Maps.text: A map is best defined as __________.
options: a scaled representation of the earth's surface, or part of it, drawn on a flat surface
a photograph of the earth's surface taken from an aircraft
a written description of the physical features of a place
a three-dimensional model of a landscape built from clay
Maps.correct_answer: a scaled representation of the earth's surface, or part of it, drawn on a flat surface

Maps.text: Which type of map shows both natural and man-made features of an area, including relief, drainage, roads, settlements and vegetation?
Maps.correct_answer: Topographical map

Maps.text: A map that shows countries, states, boundaries and capital cities is known as a __________ map.
Maps.correct_answer: political

Maps.text: Physical maps are chiefly used to show __________.
options: the distribution of rock types and mineral deposits
daily atmospheric pressure and wind systems
relief features such as mountains, plains and rivers
Maps.correct_answer: relief features such as mountains, plains and rivers

Maps.text: A thematic map is one that __________.
options: illustrates the spatial distribution of a single theme or subject, such as population or rainfall
shows only the boundaries of a country
is drawn strictly to a representative fraction of 1:50000
is used only by ships for navigation
Maps.correct_answer: illustrates the spatial distribution of a single theme or subject, such as population or rainfall

Maps.text: Geological maps are most useful to which of the following professionals?
Maps.correct_answer: Mining engineers and petroleum geologists

Maps.text: A weather map typically displays __________.
options: the boundaries of local government areas
Maps.correct_answer: isobars, wind direction and fronts

Maps.text: The scale of a map may be defined as __________.
options: the total area covered by the map
the number of colours used on the map
the direction from true north shown on the map
the ratio between a distance on the map and the corresponding distance on the ground
Maps.correct_answer: the ratio between a distance on the map and the corresponding distance on the ground

Maps.text: A statement scale expressed as '1 centimetre represents 2 kilometres' can be written as a representative fraction of __________.
A representative fraction of 1:50000 means that __________.
options: 1 cm on the map represents 50000 cm on the ground
1 km on the map represents 50000 km on the ground
the map was surveyed in the year 50000
Maps.correct_answer: 1 cm on the map represents 50000 cm on the ground

Maps.text: Which type of scale remains accurate even when a map is photocopied and enlarged or reduced in size?
Maps.correct_answer: Linear (graphical) scale

Maps.text: A representative fraction of 1:25000 is equivalent to which statement scale?
Maps.correct_answer: 1 cm represents 250 m

Maps.text: Between a map with a scale of 1:10000 and one with a scale of 1:250000, the map with the scale of 1:10000 is described as __________.
options: a large-scale map showing more detail
a small-scale map showing less detail
Maps.correct_answer: a large-scale map showing more detail

Maps.text: To measure the distance along a winding road on a map most accurately, a student should __________.
options: use a ruler to measure a straight line between the two end points
lay a piece of thread or string along the bends of the road, then measure the thread against the scale
count the number of grid squares the road passes through
Maps.correct_answer: lay a piece of thread or string along the bends of the road, then measure the thread against the scale

Maps.text: The area enclosed by an irregular boundary on a map can be estimated by __________.
options: multiplying the length by the width of the whole map
measuring only the perimeter with a piece of string
overlaying the area with a grid of equal squares and counting the squares covered
Maps.correct_answer: overlaying the area with a grid of equal squares and counting the squares covered

Maps.text: On a standard topographical map, which direction is usually at the top of the map unless stated otherwise?
Maps.correct_answer: True north

Maps.text: A bearing is best described as __________.
options: the horizontal angle measured clockwise from north to a given point, usually expressed in three figures
the height of a point above sea level
the vertical distance between two contour lines
the scale used to draw a map
Maps.correct_answer: the horizontal angle measured clockwise from north to a given point, usually expressed in three figures

Maps.text: If a point X is located due north-east of point Y, the bearing of X from Y is __________.
If the bearing of a town P from town Q is 060°, the back bearing (bearing of Q from P) is __________.
On a map, a symbol showing a small cross or a shape with a spire is most likely used to represent __________.
Maps.correct_answer: a church

Maps.text: The map symbol for a marsh or swamp typically consists of __________.
options: a series of parallel blue tufted or reed-like marks
a series of dots arranged in rows
Maps.correct_answer: a series of parallel blue tufted or reed-like marks

Maps.text: Railway lines on a topographical map are usually represented by __________.
options: a line with regular cross-hatching (tick marks) resembling a ladder
Maps.correct_answer: a line with regular cross-hatching (tick marks) resembling a ladder

Maps.text: Contour lines on a map are defined as __________.
options: lines joining places of equal rainfall
lines joining places of equal temperature
imaginary lines joining places of equal height above sea level
lines that separate one country from another
Maps.correct_answer: imaginary lines joining places of equal height above sea level

Maps.text: The vertical difference in height between two consecutive contour lines on a map is known as the __________.
Maps.correct_answer: contour interval

Maps.text: On a map, contour lines that are drawn very close together indicate __________.
Maps.correct_answer: a steep slope

Maps.text: Widely spaced contour lines on a map represent __________.
Maps.correct_answer: a gentle slope

Maps.text: A set of concentric contour circles with values increasing towards the centre represents __________.
options: a plateau edge with a cliff
Maps.correct_answer: a hill or an upland

Maps.text: A closed depression on a map, such as a crater, is distinguished from a hill on contour maps by the use of __________.
options: a different colour for the outline
a dashed instead of solid contour line
hachures (short lines) pointing inward toward the lowest point
Maps.correct_answer: hachures (short lines) pointing inward toward the lowest point

Maps.text: V-shaped contour lines that point upstream (in the direction of higher ground) on a map usually indicate __________.
Maps.correct_answer: a river valley

Maps.text: A spot height on a map refers to __________.
options: the highest contour line on the map
a point whose exact height above sea level has been measured and marked
Maps.correct_answer: a point whose exact height above sea level has been measured and marked

Maps.text: A triangulation (trigonometric) station shown on a map is used mainly for __________.
options: marking the site of a market
showing the location of a school
accurate land surveying and establishing reference points for mapping
Maps.correct_answer: accurate land surveying and establishing reference points for mapping

Maps.text: Topographical maps are especially useful to town planners because they __________.
options: provide detailed relief, drainage and settlement information needed for planning
Maps.correct_answer: provide detailed relief, drainage and settlement information needed for planning

Maps.text: Political maps are most useful for __________.
options: showing international boundaries, capital cities and administrative divisions
Maps.correct_answer: showing international boundaries, capital cities and administrative divisions

Maps.text: On a weather map, closely spaced isobars indicate __________.
options: strong winds due to a steep pressure gradient
Maps.correct_answer: strong winds due to a steep pressure gradient

Maps.text: A four-figure grid reference gives the location of __________.
options: a precise point within a grid square
the exact centre of the map
the south-west corner of a grid square
the north-east corner of the whole map
Maps.correct_answer: the south-west corner of a grid square

Maps.text: In a grid reference, the first set of figures (read first) refers to the __________.
Maps.correct_answer: eastings (vertical lines)

Maps.text: The key or legend of a map is important because it __________.
options: explains the meaning of the symbols and colours used on the map
shows the direction of true north only
gives the population of the area mapped
Maps.correct_answer: explains the meaning of the symbols and colours used on the map

Maps.text: A map drawn at a scale of 1:1000000 would be classified as a __________.
Maps.correct_answer: small-scale map

Geographic Information System GIS.text: Geographic Information System (GIS) is best defined as __________.
options: a computer-based system for capturing, storing, analysing and displaying geographically referenced data
a paper map showing only political boundaries
a device used only for taking aerial photographs
a type of compass used in fieldwork
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: a computer-based system for capturing, storing, analysing and displaying geographically referenced data

Geographic Information System GIS.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the five basic components of a GIS?
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: Folklore

Geographic Information System GIS.text: In a GIS, the physical computer equipment such as the processor, monitor, scanner and plotter is referred to as __________.
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: hardware

Geographic Information System GIS.text: GIS software is important because it provides the __________.
options: physical storage devices for the system
trained personnel who operate the system
tools and functions needed to input, manage, analyse and display spatial data
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: tools and functions needed to input, manage, analyse and display spatial data

Geographic Information System GIS.text: In the components of GIS, 'people' or 'experts' refer to __________.
options: the trained personnel who design, manage, operate and interpret the GIS
the general public who never use maps
the manufacturers of computer hardware only
the citizens whose data is captured in the system
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: the trained personnel who design, manage, operate and interpret the GIS

Geographic Information System GIS.text: The defined methods and rules by which spatial data is collected, processed and analysed in a GIS are known as __________.
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: procedures

Geographic Information System GIS.text: Which of the following best describes 'data' as a component of GIS?
options: The set of instructions written to run the computer
The physical devices used to display maps
The geographically referenced information and its attributes that are captured, stored and analysed
The trained staff who manage the system
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: The geographically referenced information and its attributes that are captured, stored and analysed

Geographic Information System GIS.text: Which of the following is a major source of data used to build a GIS database?
options: Remote sensing imagery from satellites and aircraft
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: Remote sensing imagery from satellites and aircraft

Geographic Information System GIS.text: Converting an existing paper map into digital form for use in a GIS, by tracing its features on a computer, is known as __________.
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: digitizing

Geographic Information System GIS.text: Scanning, as a source of GIS data, involves __________.
options: physically measuring distances in the field with a chain
converting paper maps or documents into digital raster images using an optical scanner
interviewing local residents about land use
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: converting paper maps or documents into digital raster images using an optical scanner

Geographic Information System GIS.text: Land surveying contributes to GIS data collection mainly by providing __________.
options: accurate ground measurements of distances, angles and elevations
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: accurate ground measurements of distances, angles and elevations

Geographic Information System GIS.text: Field investigation as a source of GIS data involves __________.
options: analysing data entirely from an office desk
physically visiting an area to observe, measure and record information directly
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: physically visiting an area to observe, measure and record information directly

Geographic Information System GIS.text: Tabular data used in a GIS refers to __________.
options: information such as statistics and attribute records arranged in rows and columns and linked to spatial features
contour lines on a topographical map
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: information such as statistics and attribute records arranged in rows and columns and linked to spatial features

Geographic Information System GIS.text: Remote sensing, as used in GIS data capture, is best described as __________.
options: measuring land boundaries using a measuring tape on site
obtaining information about the earth's surface from a distance, typically using satellites or aircraft sensors
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: obtaining information about the earth's surface from a distance, typically using satellites or aircraft sensors

Geographic Information System GIS.text: One important application of GIS in national defence is __________.
options: planning military strategy, monitoring borders and tracking troop movements
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: planning military strategy, monitoring borders and tracking troop movements

Geographic Information System GIS.text: In agriculture, GIS is applied mainly to __________.
options: monitor crop health, plan irrigation and manage land use for farming
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: monitor crop health, plan irrigation and manage land use for farming

Geographic Information System GIS.text: GIS assists urban development by enabling planners to __________.
options: analyse land use patterns, plan infrastructure and manage urban growth effectively
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: analyse land use patterns, plan infrastructure and manage urban growth effectively

Geographic Information System GIS.text: In mapping and surveying, GIS is valuable because it allows for __________.
options: the complete elimination of the need for any spatial data
faster, more accurate production and updating of maps compared to manual methods
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: faster, more accurate production and updating of maps compared to manual methods

Geographic Information System GIS.text: GIS is applied in transportation mainly to __________.
options: plan and manage road networks, optimise routes and monitor traffic flow
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: plan and manage road networks, optimise routes and monitor traffic flow

Geographic Information System GIS.text: During a national population census, GIS is useful for __________.
options: mapping enumeration areas, tracking population distribution and analysing demographic patterns
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: mapping enumeration areas, tracking population distribution and analysing demographic patterns

Geographic Information System GIS.text: One major challenge facing the effective use of GIS in West Africa is __________.
options: an excess of trained GIS professionals
too much government funding for technology
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: unreliable and inadequate power (electricity) supply

Geographic Information System GIS.text: A significant obstacle to GIS adoption in many West African countries is __________.
options: the abundance of digital maps already available
the shortage of adequately trained personnel and experts in GIS technology
too many satellites orbiting the region
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: the shortage of adequately trained personnel and experts in GIS technology

Geographic Information System GIS.text: The high cost of GIS hardware, software and data acquisition represents a challenge in West Africa often described as __________.
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: a capital or funding constraint

Geographic Information System GIS.text: Which of the following is an example of GIS hardware?
options: A digitizer or scanner used to input spatial data
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: A digitizer or scanner used to input spatial data

Geographic Information System GIS.text: Which of the following best illustrates the 'data' component rather than the 'software' component of a GIS?
options: A set of soil-type records linked to specific locations
A programme used to overlay two maps
The operating system of the computer
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: A set of soil-type records linked to specific locations

Geographic Information System GIS.text: A key advantage of GIS over traditional paper maps is that GIS __________.
options: can combine and analyse multiple layers of spatial data simultaneously
is always cheaper to produce than a paper map
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: can combine and analyse multiple layers of spatial data simultaneously

Geographic Information System GIS.text: Poor internet connectivity and inconsistent electricity in many West African institutions primarily hinder GIS by __________.
options: increasing the number of trained GIS technicians
disrupting data processing, storage and real-time analysis
reducing the cost of satellite imagery
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: disrupting data processing, storage and real-time analysis

Geographic Information System GIS.text: Which government agency function would most benefit from GIS applications in national defence and security?
options: Monitoring of borders and strategic installations
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: Monitoring of borders and strategic installations

Geographic Information System GIS.text: In GIS, 'software' typically includes tools for __________.
options: input, storage, manipulation, analysis and output of spatial data
physically surveying land with a theodolite
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: input, storage, manipulation, analysis and output of spatial data

Geographic Information System GIS.text: A GIS technician overlaying a soil map with a rainfall map to identify suitable farming zones is applying GIS to __________.
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: agriculture

Geographic Information System GIS.text: Which of the following data sources would provide the most up-to-date, large-area coverage for a GIS monitoring deforestation?
options: Oral interviews with village elders only
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: Satellite remote sensing imagery

Geographic Information System GIS.text: The process of manually tracing features from a paper map using a special digitizing tablet is called __________.
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: digitizing

Geographic Information System GIS.text: An inadequate supply of skilled GIS analysts in a region would most directly affect the GIS component known as __________.
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: people/experts

Geographic Information System GIS.text: Which of the following best explains why GIS is valuable for planning transportation routes in a fast-growing West African city?
options: It eliminates the need for roads entirely
It allows planners to analyse traffic data, road networks and land use together to optimise routes
It replaces the need for city budgets
It automatically constructs new roads without human input
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: It allows planners to analyse traffic data, road networks and land use together to optimise routes

Geographic Information System GIS.text: A national statistics office using GIS to map where different ethnic groups live based on census returns is applying GIS in which sector?
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: Census and demographic analysis

Geographic Information System GIS.text: Which statement about GIS challenges in West Africa is most accurate?
options: Every West African country has unlimited funding for GIS projects
There is no shortage of GIS experts anywhere in the region
Electricity supply is never a limiting factor for GIS use
Limited capital investment restricts the purchase of GIS hardware and software in many institutions
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: Limited capital investment restricts the purchase of GIS hardware and software in many institutions

Geographic Information System GIS.text: Field investigation is often combined with remote sensing data in GIS mainly to __________.
options: verify and ground-truth the information obtained from satellite images
reduce the accuracy of the final dataset
eliminate the need for any computer hardware
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: verify and ground-truth the information obtained from satellite images

Geographic Information System GIS.text: Which of the following best distinguishes 'procedures' from 'data' in a GIS?
options: Procedures and data mean exactly the same thing in GIS
Procedures are the defined methods/workflows used, while data is the actual information being processed
Procedures refer only to hardware maintenance schedules
Data refers only to the people who operate the system
Geographic Information System GIS.correct_answer: Procedures are the defined methods/workflows used, while data is the actual information being processed

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: A bar graph is a statistical diagram in which __________.
options: data values are represented by rectangular bars whose length or height is proportional to the value
data values are represented by circles of varying size
data values are shown using dots scattered across a map
data values are joined by a continuous line
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: data values are represented by rectangular bars whose length or height is proportional to the value

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: In a simple bar graph, the width of each bar __________.
options: must vary according to the value being represented
is usually kept constant, as only the length/height carries meaning
represents the total sum of all the data
must always equal the height of the bar
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: is usually kept constant, as only the length/height carries meaning

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: A compound (multiple) bar graph is most useful when a student wants to __________.
options: show only one variable for one year
show the exact geographical location of a place
compare two or more related sets of data side by side for the same category
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: compare two or more related sets of data side by side for the same category

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: A divided (component) bar graph differs from a simple bar graph in that it __________.
options: shows only a single value with no subdivisions
cannot be used to show percentages
splits each bar into segments to show the components that make up the total
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: splits each bar into segments to show the components that make up the total

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: A line graph is particularly suitable for showing __________.
options: trends or changes in a variable over a continuous period, such as time
the exact location of towns on a map
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: trends or changes in a variable over a continuous period, such as time

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: When plotting a line graph of monthly rainfall figures, the horizontal (x) axis usually represents __________.
options: the amount of rainfall in millimetres
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: the months of the year

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: A major limitation of a simple line graph is that it __________.
options: cannot show trends over time at all
is never used in climate studies
may become cluttered and hard to read when too many variables are plotted on the same axes
cannot be drawn on graph paper
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: may become cluttered and hard to read when too many variables are plotted on the same axes

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: A flow chart (or flow-line map) uses arrows or lines of varying width mainly to represent __________.
options: the height of land above sea level
the average annual temperature of a region
the boundary of a local government area
the volume or direction of movement of goods, people or traffic between places
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: the volume or direction of movement of goods, people or traffic between places

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: On a flow-line map, the thickness of the flow line is generally proportional to __________.
options: the quantity or volume being transported
the distance between the two places
the population of the destination only
the scale of the base map
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: the quantity or volume being transported

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: A dot map is a statistical map in which __________.
options: circles of different sizes are used to compare totals
each dot represents a fixed quantity, and dots are placed within areas to show distribution, e.g. population
colours are shaded to represent density ranges
lines join points of equal value
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: each dot represents a fixed quantity, and dots are placed within areas to show distribution, e.g. population

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: One key step in constructing a dot map is to __________.
options: use dots of different colours for the same variable
avoid using any legend or key
decide on a suitable dot value (the quantity each dot represents) before plotting
place all dots in a single cluster regardless of distribution
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: decide on a suitable dot value (the quantity each dot represents) before plotting

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: A major disadvantage of dot maps is that __________.
options: they are always more accurate than any other statistical map
they cannot show spatial distribution at all
they require no key or legend to interpret
it can be difficult to determine the exact value represented in areas of dense dot clustering
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: it can be difficult to determine the exact value represented in areas of dense dot clustering

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: Proportional circles on a statistical map are used to __________.
options: represent quantities for different places using circles whose area is proportional to the value
show the direction of wind flow only
represent contour lines on relief maps
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: represent quantities for different places using circles whose area is proportional to the value

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: In constructing proportional circles, the radius of each circle is typically calculated using the __________.
options: cube of the value it represents
square root of the value it represents
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: square root of the value it represents

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: Divided (pie) proportional circles combine the features of a proportional circle and a __________.
options: divided bar graph, since each circle is split into sectors representing components
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: divided bar graph, since each circle is split into sectors representing components

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: A choropleth (density/shading) map represents statistical data by __________.
options: drawing lines that join points of equal value across a continuous surface
placing dots of equal value across the map
using bars of varying height at fixed points
using different shades or colours to represent value ranges within predefined areas such as regions or states
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: using different shades or colours to represent value ranges within predefined areas such as regions or states

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: On a choropleth map, generally darker shading is conventionally used to represent __________.
options: higher values of the variable being mapped
lower values of the variable being mapped
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: higher values of the variable being mapped

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: A significant limitation of choropleth maps is that __________.
options: they can never be shaded or coloured
they assume uniform distribution of a value across an entire administrative unit, which may be misleading
they cannot be used to show population density
they require the use of dots instead of shading
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: they assume uniform distribution of a value across an entire administrative unit, which may be misleading

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: An isopleth map (such as an isohyet or isotherm map) is constructed by __________.
options: shading whole administrative regions a single colour
placing bars of different heights at each location
joining places of exactly equal value with a continuous line
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: joining places of exactly equal value with a continuous line

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: Isohyets are isopleths that join places having equal __________.
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: rainfall

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: Isotherms are lines on a map joining places of equal __________.
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: temperature

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: Contour lines used to show relief are technically a form of isopleth joining places of equal __________.
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: height above sea level

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: Isobars on a weather map join places of equal __________.
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: atmospheric pressure

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: When choosing an appropriate statistical diagram to compare the population of five different towns for one particular year, the most suitable choice would be a __________.
options: line graph showing trends over decades
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: simple bar graph

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: To show the change in a country's export earnings over a 20-year period, the most appropriate diagram would be a __________.
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: line graph

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: To show the volume of migrants moving from rural areas to different cities, the most suitable diagram is a __________.
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: flow-line map

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: To show the density of population across the different states of a country, the most appropriate map is a __________.
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: choropleth (shading) map

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: To show rainfall distribution as a continuous surface across a whole country, the most appropriate map type is an __________.
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: isohyet (isopleth) map

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: To compare the composition of exports (percentage contribution of each crop) for a single country in one year, the best diagram is a __________.
options: divided (component) bar graph or pie chart
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: divided (component) bar graph or pie chart

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: A key advantage of proportional circles over simple bar graphs when comparing quantities at specific locations is that circles __________.
options: never require any calculation to construct
can be placed directly at the exact location on a map, preserving spatial information
must always be the same size regardless of value
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: can be placed directly at the exact location on a map, preserving spatial information

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: One disadvantage shared by both dot maps and proportional circle maps is that __________.
options: they are unsuitable for showing any spatial data
they cannot be drawn on a base map
reading precise values directly from the map can be difficult without careful reference to the key
they never require a scale or key
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: reading precise values directly from the map can be difficult without careful reference to the key

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: A pictogram (or pictograph) represents statistical data using __________.
options: small pictures or symbols, each representing a fixed quantity of the item being measured
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: small pictures or symbols, each representing a fixed quantity of the item being measured

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: In constructing a line graph, values are plotted as points which are then __________.
options: joined by straight lines to show the trend from one period to the next
shaded in with a single solid colour
replaced with bars of equal height
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: joined by straight lines to show the trend from one period to the next

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: A histogram differs from a simple bar graph mainly in that a histogram __________.
options: is used only for showing rainfall on a map
is used for continuous data and the bars are drawn touching each other without gaps
always has bars of the same colour as a pie chart
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: is used for continuous data and the bars are drawn touching each other without gaps

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: A major advantage of statistical diagrams over raw numerical tables is that diagrams __________.
options: always contain more precise figures than tables
eliminate the need for a title or key
present data visually, making patterns, trends and comparisons easier to grasp at a glance
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: present data visually, making patterns, trends and comparisons easier to grasp at a glance

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: When constructing any statistical map or diagram, which of the following is essential for correct interpretation?
options: The use of as many colours as possible regardless of meaning
Omitting the source of the data
A clear title, key/legend and, where relevant, a scale
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: A clear title, key/legend and, where relevant, a scale

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: A flow chart showing trade between two countries with an unusually thick arrow suggests __________.
options: a very large volume of trade
a very small volume of trade
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: a very large volume of trade

Statistical Maps and Diagrams.text: Isopleth maps are generally considered less suitable than choropleth maps when __________.
options: the phenomenon being mapped varies continuously across space, such as temperature
the data is only available as totals for defined administrative units rather than as continuous point readings
there is an abundance of weather station readings across the area
the map needs to show a smooth, continuous surface
Statistical Maps and Diagrams.correct_answer: the data is only available as totals for defined administrative units rather than as continuous point readings

The Earth and the Solar System.text: Latitude is best defined as

Denudational Processes.text: Deflation, a process of wind erosion, refers to the
options: Removal and lifting of loose fine particles such as sand and dust by wind
Grinding of rock surfaces by wind-blown sand
Deposition of sand to form dunes
Dissolving of rock minerals by moisture in the air
Denudational Processes.correct_answer: Removal and lifting of loose fine particles such as sand and dust by wind

Denudational Processes.text: Wind abrasion is the process by which
options: Loose surface material is lifted and blown away by wind
Rock surfaces are worn down by the sandblasting effect of wind-carried particles
Soluble rocks are dissolved by moisture
Denudational Processes.correct_answer: Rock surfaces are worn down by the sandblasting effect of wind-carried particles

Denudational Processes.text: A barchan is a type of sand dune characterised by a
options: Long, narrow, straight ridge parallel to the wind direction
Crescent shape with horns pointing in the direction the wind is blowing
Denudational Processes.correct_answer: Crescent shape with horns pointing in the direction the wind is blowing

Denudational Processes.text: A seif dune, unlike a barchan dune, is
options: Long and narrow, aligned parallel to the prevailing wind direction
Denudational Processes.correct_answer: Long and narrow, aligned parallel to the prevailing wind direction

Denudational Processes.text: In coastal (wave) erosion, hydraulic action refers to
options: The compression and force of trapped air and water breaking down cracks in cliffs
The grinding of rock fragments against the cliff face
The dissolving of soluble rocks by seawater
The wearing down of transported pebbles through collision
Denudational Processes.correct_answer: The compression and force of trapped air and water breaking down cracks in cliffs

Denudational Processes.text: A wave-cut platform is a coastal landform formed by
options: The deposition of sand along a shoreline
The continued erosion and retreat of a cliff, leaving a gently sloping rock surface at its base
The accumulation of shingle to form a ridge
The solution of limestone by underground water
Denudational Processes.correct_answer: The continued erosion and retreat of a cliff, leaving a gently sloping rock surface at its base

Denudational Processes.text: A spit is a coastal depositional landform that
options: Is a steep rocky cliff formed by wave erosion
Is a cave formed by wave action at the base of a cliff
Is a narrow ridge of sand or shingle extending from the coast into open water, often with a curved end
Is a flat platform exposed at low tide
Denudational Processes.correct_answer: Is a narrow ridge of sand or shingle extending from the coast into open water, often with a curved end

Climate.text: Climate is best defined as the
options: Average weather condition of a place over a long period, usually 30 years or more
Day-to-day state of the atmosphere at a place
Total rainfall received by a region in a single year
Temperature recorded at a place in one day
Climate.correct_answer: Average weather condition of a place over a long period, usually 30 years or more

Climate.text: Which of the following is an element of climate?
Climate.correct_answer: Humidity

Climate.text: Rainfall that results when warm moist air is forced to rise over a mountain range is known as
Climate.correct_answer: Relief (orographic) rainfall

Climate.text: Convectional rainfall is caused mainly by
options: Air being forced to rise over highlands
Warm and cold air masses meeting along a front
Onshore winds carrying moisture inland seasonally
Intense surface heating causing moist air to rise, cool and condense
Climate.correct_answer: Intense surface heating causing moist air to rise, cool and condense

Climate.text: Atmospheric pressure is measured using an instrument called a
Climate.correct_answer: Barometer

Climate.text: The instrument used to measure wind speed is the
Climate.correct_answer: Anemometer

Climate.text: Relative humidity refers to the
options: Total amount of water vapour that can be held by air at any temperature
Amount of rainfall received in a given period
Percentage ratio of the actual amount of water vapour in the air to the maximum it can hold at that temperature
Rate at which water evaporates from open surfaces
Climate.correct_answer: Percentage ratio of the actual amount of water vapour in the air to the maximum it can hold at that temperature

Climate.text: Insolation refers to
options: The scattering of sunlight by clouds
The reflection of solar radiation back into space
The amount of rainfall received from convectional storms
Incoming solar radiation received at the earth's surface
Climate.correct_answer: Incoming solar radiation received at the earth's surface

Climate.text: Clouds form mainly as a result of
options: Condensation of water vapour around tiny particles (condensation nuclei) in the atmosphere
Direct evaporation of water from the soil surface
Rapid cooling of the ocean surface
The scattering of sunlight in the upper atmosphere
Climate.correct_answer: Condensation of water vapour around tiny particles (condensation nuclei) in the atmosphere

Climate.text: Places near the equator generally experience higher temperatures than places near the poles mainly because of
options: The angle at which the sun's rays strike the earth's surface, which varies with latitude
Differences in the amount of cloud cover
Climate.correct_answer: The angle at which the sun's rays strike the earth's surface, which varies with latitude

Climate.text: Temperature generally decreases with increasing altitude mainly because
options: Higher places are farther from the equator
The air at higher altitudes is less dense and holds less heat
Climate.correct_answer: The air at higher altitudes is less dense and holds less heat

Climate.text: A warm ocean current flowing along a coast tends to
options: Lower the temperature of nearby coastal areas
Reduce the amount of rainfall in the region
Have no effect on the climate of nearby land
Raise the temperature and increase rainfall of nearby coastal areas
Climate.correct_answer: Raise the temperature and increase rainfall of nearby coastal areas

Climate.text: A land breeze occurs
options: At night, when the land cools faster than the sea and air moves from land to sea
During the day, when the land heats faster than the sea and air moves from sea to land
When cold ocean currents meet warm currents
Climate.correct_answer: At night, when the land cools faster than the sea and air moves from land to sea

Climate.text: A sea breeze occurs mainly because, during the day,
options: The sea heats up faster than the land
The land heats up faster than the sea, causing air to rise over land and be replaced by cooler air from the sea
The land cools faster than the sea
Pressure over the sea becomes lower than over the land at night
Climate.correct_answer: The land heats up faster than the sea, causing air to rise over land and be replaced by cooler air from the sea

Climate.text: Continentality refers to the effect on climate of
options: A location's height above sea level
A location's distance from the equator
A location's distance from the moderating influence of the sea, leading to greater temperature extremes
The direction a slope faces relative to the sun
Climate.correct_answer: A location's distance from the moderating influence of the sea, leading to greater temperature extremes

Climate.text: Aspect, as a factor affecting local climate, refers to
options: The height of a place above sea level
The distance of a place from the sea
The general wind pattern of a region
The direction a slope faces, which affects the amount of sunlight and warmth it receives
Climate.correct_answer: The direction a slope faces, which affects the amount of sunlight and warmth it receives

Climate.text: The equatorial climate type is characterised by
options: High temperatures and heavy rainfall throughout the year with no marked dry season
A long dry season and a short wet season with moderate rainfall
Very low rainfall and extreme temperature ranges between day and night
Cold winters and warm, wet summers
Climate.correct_answer: High temperatures and heavy rainfall throughout the year with no marked dry season

Climate.text: The tropical continental (Sudan type) climate is characterised mainly by
options: Rainfall throughout the year with no dry season
A distinct wet and dry season, with rainfall concentrated in the summer months
Climate.correct_answer: A distinct wet and dry season, with rainfall concentrated in the summer months

Climate.text: The hot desert climate is characterised by
options: Heavy annual rainfall and high humidity
Cool summers and mild, wet winters
Very low and unreliable rainfall with a wide diurnal (day-night) range of temperature
Reliable convectional rainfall throughout the year
Climate.correct_answer: Very low and unreliable rainfall with a wide diurnal (day-night) range of temperature

Climate.text: The tropical marine climate differs from the tropical continental climate mainly in that it
options: Has a much wider temperature range between seasons
Is found only in the interior of continents
Experiences fairly reliable rainfall throughout the year due to maritime influence
Climate.correct_answer: Experiences fairly reliable rainfall throughout the year due to maritime influence

Climate.text: The Mediterranean climate type is characterised by
options: Warm, dry summers and mild, wet winters
Hot, wet summers and cold, dry winters
Uniformly cold temperatures throughout the year
Heavy rainfall in all seasons with no dry period
Climate.correct_answer: Warm, dry summers and mild, wet winters

Climate.text: The cool temperate western margin (British type) climate is noted for
options: Very low rainfall and hot summers
Mild temperatures and rainfall well distributed throughout the year
A pronounced dry season in summer
Climate.correct_answer: Mild temperatures and rainfall well distributed throughout the year

Climate.text: The warm temperate eastern margin (China type) climate experiences
options: Hot, wet summers influenced by monsoon winds and cool, drier winters
Permanent snow cover throughout the year
Climate.correct_answer: Hot, wet summers influenced by monsoon winds and cool, drier winters

Climate.text: The cool temperate continental (Siberian) climate is characterised by
options: Small annual temperature range and abundant rainfall
Rainfall evenly distributed with no temperature extremes
Very cold winters, warm summers, and a large annual temperature range
Climate.correct_answer: Very cold winters, warm summers, and a large annual temperature range

Climate.text: The Greek system of climate classification divides the earth into climatic zones mainly on the basis of
options: Latitude and the amount of heat received from the sun (torrid, temperate and frigid zones)
The type of natural vegetation found in a region
Climate.correct_answer: Latitude and the amount of heat received from the sun (torrid, temperate and frigid zones)

Climate.text: In the Greek classification of climate, the torrid zone refers to the
options: Zone found between latitudes 40 degrees and 66.5 degrees
Hot zone located between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn
Cold zone found around the poles
Zone with the greatest temperature range on earth
Climate.correct_answer: Hot zone located between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn

Climate.text: The frigid zones in the Greek classification of climate are located
options: Between the tropics and the polar circles
Around the North and South Poles, beyond the polar circles
Climate.correct_answer: Around the North and South Poles, beyond the polar circles

Climate.text: The Köppen system of climate classification groups climates mainly using
options: Only the length of daylight hours
The type of rocks found in a region
Letter codes based on temperature and precipitation characteristics
Climate.correct_answer: Letter codes based on temperature and precipitation characteristics

Climate.text: In the Köppen classification, climate type "A" represents
options: Tropical (humid) climates with high temperatures throughout the year
Climate.correct_answer: Tropical (humid) climates with high temperatures throughout the year

Climate.text: In the Köppen classification, climate type "B" represents
options: Dry climates, including arid deserts and semi-arid steppes
Climate.correct_answer: Dry climates, including arid deserts and semi-arid steppes

Climate.text: In the Köppen classification, climate type "E" represents
options: Polar climates with very low temperatures throughout the year
Climate.correct_answer: Polar climates with very low temperatures throughout the year

Climate.text: Climate change refers to
options: The normal daily variation in weather conditions
A single unusually hot or cold day
The difference between weather in the morning and evening
A long-term, significant alteration in global or regional climate patterns, especially temperature and rainfall
Climate.correct_answer: A long-term, significant alteration in global or regional climate patterns, especially temperature and rainfall

Climate.text: The greenhouse effect, a major contributor to global climate change, is caused mainly by
options: The build-up of gases such as carbon dioxide and methane that trap heat in the atmosphere
The reduction of wind speed over the oceans
Climate.correct_answer: The build-up of gases such as carbon dioxide and methane that trap heat in the atmosphere

Climate.text: Deforestation contributes to climate change mainly because it
options: Increases the amount of oxygen absorbed by trees
Reduces the number of trees available to absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere
Increases rainfall in the affected area
Climate.correct_answer: Reduces the number of trees available to absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere

Climate.text: A major human activity that increases greenhouse gas concentration in the atmosphere is
options: The burning of fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas
Climate.correct_answer: The burning of fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas

Climate.text: Which of the following is a major effect of global climate change?
options: A permanent decrease in global temperatures
Increased snowfall in all tropical regions
A decrease in the frequency of extreme weather events
Rising sea levels due to melting ice caps and glaciers
Climate.correct_answer: Rising sea levels due to melting ice caps and glaciers

Climate.text: In West Africa, one notable effect of climate change is
options: The southward expansion of desert conditions (desertification) in the Sahel region
A permanent increase in forest cover across the region
A steady drop in average temperatures
The disappearance of the harmattan wind
Climate.correct_answer: The southward expansion of desert conditions (desertification) in the Sahel region

Climate.text: One effective way of mitigating (reducing) the effects of climate change is
options: Increasing the use of fossil fuels for energy
Planting more trees (afforestation) to absorb carbon dioxide
Climate.correct_answer: Planting more trees (afforestation) to absorb carbon dioxide

Climate.text: Which of the following measures would best help reduce greenhouse gas emissions?
options: Expanding the use of coal-fired power plants
Increasing the use of renewable energy sources such as solar and wind power
Climate.correct_answer: Increasing the use of renewable energy sources such as solar and wind power

Environmental Resources.text: A renewable resource is one that
options: Can be replenished naturally within a relatively short period of time
Once used up, cannot be replaced within a human lifetime
Is found only in tropical regions
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Can be replenished naturally within a relatively short period of time

Environmental Resources.text: A non-renewable resource is best described as one that
options: Takes millions of years to form and cannot be replaced within a human timescale once exhausted
Is found only in the atmosphere
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Takes millions of years to form and cannot be replaced within a human timescale once exhausted

Environmental Resources.text: Which of the following is an example of a renewable resource?
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Solar energy

Environmental Resources.text: Which of the following is an example of a non-renewable resource?
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Petroleum (crude oil)

Environmental Resources.text: Vegetation resources refer to
options: Plant life such as forests, grasslands and other natural plant cover that provide economic and environmental benefits
Mineral deposits found beneath forested land
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Plant life such as forests, grasslands and other natural plant cover that provide economic and environmental benefits

Environmental Resources.text: Which of the following is NOT a major use of vegetation resources?
options: Extraction of crude oil for fuel
Regulation of climate through absorption of carbon dioxide
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Extraction of crude oil for fuel

Environmental Resources.text: A major consequence of the excessive removal of vegetation (deforestation) is
options: Increased soil erosion due to exposed, unprotected soil
Increased rainfall infiltration into the soil
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Increased soil erosion due to exposed, unprotected soil

Environmental Resources.text: Surface water resources include all of the following EXCEPT
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Aquifers (groundwater stored in rock)

Environmental Resources.text: Groundwater refers to water that
options: Has infiltrated the soil and is stored in permeable rock layers (aquifers) beneath the earth's surface
Flows on the surface as rivers and streams
Is stored in artificial reservoirs behind dams
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Has infiltrated the soil and is stored in permeable rock layers (aquifers) beneath the earth's surface

Environmental Resources.text: Which of the following is a major use of water resources?
options: Irrigation of farmland for crop production
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Irrigation of farmland for crop production

Environmental Resources.text: A major cause of water resource pollution in many West African communities is
options: Indiscriminate dumping of industrial and domestic waste into rivers and streams
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Indiscriminate dumping of industrial and domestic waste into rivers and streams

Environmental Resources.text: Mineral resources refer to
options: Gases that make up the atmosphere
Naturally occurring inorganic substances extracted from the earth's crust for economic use
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Naturally occurring inorganic substances extracted from the earth's crust for economic use

Environmental Resources.text: Minerals such as gold, bauxite and iron ore are classified as
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Metallic minerals

Environmental Resources.text: Which of the following is an example of a non-metallic mineral resource?
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Limestone

Environmental Resources.text: Petroleum, coal and natural gas are collectively classified as
options: Fossil fuel (mineral) resources, formed from the remains of organisms over millions of years
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Fossil fuel (mineral) resources, formed from the remains of organisms over millions of years

Environmental Resources.text: A major environmental problem commonly associated with surface (open-cast) mineral mining is
options: Land degradation, including large pits and loss of vegetation cover
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Land degradation, including large pits and loss of vegetation cover

Environmental Resources.text: Atmospheric resources refer to
options: The gases and climatic elements of the atmosphere, such as oxygen, carbon dioxide, sunlight and wind, that support life and economic activity
Mineral ores found beneath the earth's surface
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: The gases and climatic elements of the atmosphere, such as oxygen, carbon dioxide, sunlight and wind, that support life and economic activity

Environmental Resources.text: Which of the following best illustrates the use of an atmospheric resource?
options: Mining of gold from underground deposits
Harnessing wind energy to generate electricity
Irrigation of farmland with river water
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Harnessing wind energy to generate electricity

Environmental Resources.text: The ozone layer, an important part of atmospheric resources, mainly functions to
options: Absorb and filter out most of the sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Absorb and filter out most of the sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation

Environmental Resources.text: A major cause of air pollution as it affects atmospheric resources is
options: Use of solar panels for electricity generation
Emission of smoke and harmful gases from industries and vehicles
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Emission of smoke and harmful gases from industries and vehicles

Environmental Resources.text: Sustainable use of environmental resources means
options: Using resources in a way that meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
Exploiting resources as quickly as possible for maximum immediate profit
Using only non-renewable resources for development
Avoiding the use of any natural resource altogether
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Using resources in a way that meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs

Environmental Resources.text: Which of the following practices best supports the sustainable management of vegetation resources?
options: Selective logging combined with reforestation programmes
Clearing entire forests for a single crop without replanting
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Selective logging combined with reforestation programmes

Environmental Resources.text: An effective measure for the sustainable management of water resources is
options: Discharging untreated sewage directly into rivers
Constructing water treatment plants and regulating water use through conservation practices
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Constructing water treatment plants and regulating water use through conservation practices

Environmental Resources.text: Sustainable management of mineral resources includes
options: Extracting minerals without any regard for land reclamation
Ignoring environmental impact assessments before mining
Allowing unregulated artisanal mining in protected areas
Rehabilitating and reclaiming mined-out land after extraction
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Rehabilitating and reclaiming mined-out land after extraction

Environmental Resources.text: Resources such as solar energy and wind, which are continuously available regardless of use, are best described as
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Flow (renewable) resources

Environmental Resources.text: A resource that exists in a fixed quantity and diminishes permanently with continued extraction is known as an
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Exhaustible (non-renewable) resource

Environmental Resources.text: Which of the following is a direct economic benefit derived from forest vegetation resources?
options: Production of timber, rubber and medicinal plant extracts
Extraction of bauxite for aluminium production
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Production of timber, rubber and medicinal plant extracts

Environmental Resources.text: Rivers serve as an important water resource in West Africa mainly because they
options: Contain deposits of coal and petroleum
Provide habitats exclusively for desert animals
Are the main source of atmospheric oxygen
Can be dammed to generate hydroelectric power, in addition to supplying water for irrigation and domestic use
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Can be dammed to generate hydroelectric power, in addition to supplying water for irrigation and domestic use

Environmental Resources.text: A country in West Africa well known for large deposits of petroleum as a mineral resource is
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Nigeria

Environmental Resources.text: Ghana is particularly noted for its large deposits of the mineral resource known as
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Gold

Environmental Resources.text: Solar energy, as an atmospheric resource, is increasingly used in West Africa mainly for
options: Generating electricity through solar panels, especially in rural areas without grid power
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Generating electricity through solar panels, especially in rural areas without grid power

Environmental Resources.text: The overexploitation of environmental resources, without regard for sustainability, generally leads to
options: Increased resource availability for future generations
Resource depletion, environmental degradation and reduced availability for future use
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Resource depletion, environmental degradation and reduced availability for future use

Environmental Resources.text: Forests are often described as "carbon sinks" because they
options: Absorb and store carbon dioxide from the atmosphere through photosynthesis
Release large amounts of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere
Prevent all forms of soil erosion completely
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Absorb and store carbon dioxide from the atmosphere through photosynthesis

Environmental Resources.text: A major cause of water scarcity in many parts of West Africa is
options: Erratic rainfall patterns combined with poor water management and population pressure
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Erratic rainfall patterns combined with poor water management and population pressure

Environmental Resources.text: Because minerals are non-renewable resources, their exploitation should be guided mainly by
options: Maximising extraction speed regardless of remaining reserves
Ignoring the needs of future generations
Careful and efficient use, along with recycling, to conserve reserves for the future
Avoiding any form of processing after extraction
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Careful and efficient use, along with recycling, to conserve reserves for the future

Environmental Resources.text: Wind, as an atmospheric resource, is harnessed mainly through the use of
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Wind turbines to generate electricity

Environmental Resources.text: Afforestation programmes are important for sustainable resource management mainly because they help to
options: Restore degraded land, reduce desertification and maintain the balance of atmospheric gases
Increase the rate of mineral extraction
Reduce the amount of rainfall in an area
Eliminate the need for water conservation
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Restore degraded land, reduce desertification and maintain the balance of atmospheric gases

Environmental Resources.text: Which of the following best describes an integrated approach to managing environmental resources sustainably?
options: Focusing exclusively on mineral extraction while ignoring vegetation and water resources
Coordinating the conservation and use of vegetation, water, mineral and atmospheric resources together for long-term benefit
Allowing each resource to be managed independently without any regulation
Prioritising short-term economic gain over environmental protection
Environmental Resources.correct_answer: Coordinating the conservation and use of vegetation, water, mineral and atmospheric resources together for long-term benefit

Environmental Hazards.text: Soil erosion is best defined as the process by which:
options: soil nutrients are added to the land
soil is compacted by heavy machinery
the top fertile layer of soil is removed by agents such as water and wind
rocks are broken down into soil particles
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: the top fertile layer of soil is removed by agents such as water and wind

Environmental Hazards.text: Which of the following is NOT considered a major agent of soil erosion?
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: Ocean currents

Environmental Hazards.text: Sheet erosion refers to:
options: the formation of deep channels in the soil
the removal of a thin, uniform layer of topsoil over a wide area by rainwater
the blowing away of soil particles by strong wind
the collapse of river banks during floods
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: the removal of a thin, uniform layer of topsoil over a wide area by rainwater

Environmental Hazards.text: Rill erosion is characterized by:
options: wide, shallow removal of soil across a field
formation of large, deep channels that cannot be removed by ploughing
removal of soil by wave action along coasts
formation of small, shallow channels that can be smoothed out by ploughing
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: formation of small, shallow channels that can be smoothed out by ploughing

Environmental Hazards.text: Gully erosion differs from rill erosion mainly because gully erosion:
options: produces channels too deep and wide to be removed by ordinary ploughing
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: produces channels too deep and wide to be removed by ordinary ploughing

Environmental Hazards.text: Wind erosion is most severe in areas that are:
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: dry, bare, and sparsely vegetated

Environmental Hazards.text: One major effect of soil erosion on agriculture is:
options: reduction in crop yield due to loss of fertile topsoil
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: reduction in crop yield due to loss of fertile topsoil

Environmental Hazards.text: Contour ploughing helps to control soil erosion by:
options: increasing the speed of surface runoff
ploughing along the slope to channel water downhill quickly
removing vegetation cover from the land
ploughing across the slope to slow down runoff and reduce soil loss
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: ploughing across the slope to slow down runoff and reduce soil loss

Environmental Hazards.text: Terracing as a soil conservation method is most useful on:
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: steep hillsides and slopes

Environmental Hazards.text: Planting trees to reduce the impact of soil erosion is known as:
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: afforestation

Environmental Hazards.text: A major human activity that accelerates soil erosion is:
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: deforestation for farming and logging

Environmental Hazards.text: Splash erosion occurs when:
options: wind lifts soil particles into the air
raindrops strike bare soil and dislodge soil particles
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: raindrops strike bare soil and dislodge soil particles

Environmental Hazards.text: Which farming practice is most likely to accelerate soil erosion?
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: Overgrazing by livestock

Environmental Hazards.text: Drought can best be defined as:
options: a prolonged period of abnormally low rainfall leading to water shortage
a short period of light rainfall
an annual dry season occurring predictably
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: a prolonged period of abnormally low rainfall leading to water shortage

Environmental Hazards.text: A major cause of drought is:
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: persistent failure of seasonal rains

Environmental Hazards.text: One of the most serious effects of drought is:
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: famine due to crop failure

Environmental Hazards.text: An effective drought management strategy is:
options: construction of irrigation schemes and dams for water storage
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: construction of irrigation schemes and dams for water storage

Environmental Hazards.text: The region of West Africa most prone to recurrent drought is the:
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: Sahel zone

Environmental Hazards.text: Water harvesting as a drought management technique involves:
options: collecting and storing rainwater for use during dry periods
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: collecting and storing rainwater for use during dry periods

Environmental Hazards.text: Drought most directly affects livestock farming by:
options: causing death of animals due to lack of water and pasture
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: causing death of animals due to lack of water and pasture

Environmental Hazards.text: Desertification is best described as:
options: the natural formation of deserts through volcanic activity
the conversion of deserts into farmland
the process by which fertile or semi-arid land becomes increasingly arid and desert-like
the annual flooding of dry lands
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: the process by which fertile or semi-arid land becomes increasingly arid and desert-like

Environmental Hazards.text: A major human cause of desertification in the Sahel is:
options: overgrazing by livestock beyond the carrying capacity of the land
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: overgrazing by livestock beyond the carrying capacity of the land

Environmental Hazards.text: Which of the following also contributes to desertification?
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: Excessive deforestation for fuelwood

Environmental Hazards.text: Besides human activities, desertification can also be caused by:
options: long-term climatic changes leading to reduced rainfall
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: long-term climatic changes leading to reduced rainfall

Environmental Hazards.text: A key effect of desertification is:
options: loss of vegetation cover and reduction in agricultural productivity
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: loss of vegetation cover and reduction in agricultural productivity

Environmental Hazards.text: Shelterbelts help control desertification mainly by:
options: breaking the force of wind and reducing soil/sand movement
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: breaking the force of wind and reducing soil/sand movement

Environmental Hazards.text: Which of the following Sahelian countries is most affected by desertification?
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: Mauritania

Environmental Hazards.text: A major regional effort to combat desertification in the Sahel is the:
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: Great Green Wall initiative

Environmental Hazards.text: Flooding occurs when:
options: rainfall is below average for a long period
water overflows the normal confines of a river or accumulates on land that is usually dry
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: water overflows the normal confines of a river or accumulates on land that is usually dry

Environmental Hazards.text: A major cause of flooding is:
options: heavy and continuous rainfall exceeding the drainage capacity of an area
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: heavy and continuous rainfall exceeding the drainage capacity of an area

Environmental Hazards.text: Urban flooding is often worsened by:
options: blockage of drains and channels with poorly disposed refuse
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: blockage of drains and channels with poorly disposed refuse

Environmental Hazards.text: One major social effect of flooding is:
options: displacement of people from their homes and loss of property
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: displacement of people from their homes and loss of property

Environmental Hazards.text: An effective structural measure to control flooding is:
options: construction of dams, dykes and embankments along rivers
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: construction of dams, dykes and embankments along rivers

Environmental Hazards.text: Dredging and widening of river channels helps control flooding by:
options: increasing the carrying capacity of the river channel
reducing the volume of water a river can carry
blocking the flow of water completely
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: increasing the carrying capacity of the river channel

Environmental Hazards.text: Pollution can be defined as:
options: the natural cycling of nutrients in an ecosystem
the introduction of harmful substances or contaminants into the environment causing adverse effects
the planting of trees to conserve soil
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: the introduction of harmful substances or contaminants into the environment causing adverse effects

Environmental Hazards.text: A major source of air pollution is:
options: smoke and gases emitted from vehicles and industries
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: smoke and gases emitted from vehicles and industries

Environmental Hazards.text: Water pollution is commonly caused by:
options: planting of trees along river banks
discharge of industrial effluents and sewage into rivers and streams
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: discharge of industrial effluents and sewage into rivers and streams

Environmental Hazards.text: A major source of land pollution is:
options: improper disposal of solid waste and refuse
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: improper disposal of solid waste and refuse

Environmental Hazards.text: Which of the following is an effective measure for controlling pollution?
options: Enforcement of environmental laws and proper waste treatment/disposal
Environmental Hazards.correct_answer: Enforcement of environmental laws and proper waste treatment/disposal

Environmental Conservation.text: Environmental conservation refers to:
options: the total exploitation of natural resources for immediate profit
the complete prohibition of the use of natural resources
the wise use, protection, and management of natural resources to prevent depletion and degradation
the process of converting forests into farmland
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: the wise use, protection, and management of natural resources to prevent depletion and degradation

Environmental Conservation.text: Afforestation is best defined as:
options: the planting of trees in an area that previously had no forest cover
the cutting down of trees for timber
the burning of forest vegetation to prepare land for farming
the removal of tree stumps from farmland
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: the planting of trees in an area that previously had no forest cover

Environmental Conservation.text: Reforestation refers to:
options: planting trees in an area that never had forest cover before
the replanting of trees in an area where forest had previously been cleared
clearing of forest land for agricultural use
harvesting of mature trees for export
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: the replanting of trees in an area where forest had previously been cleared

Environmental Conservation.text: Crop rotation as a soil conservation method involves:
options: growing the same crop continuously on the same piece of land
leaving farmland completely bare between planting seasons
growing different crops in a planned sequence on the same land to maintain soil fertility
planting crops only during the dry season
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: growing different crops in a planned sequence on the same land to maintain soil fertility

Environmental Conservation.text: Mulching helps conserve soil by:
options: covering the soil surface with organic material to reduce evaporation and erosion
removing all vegetation cover from the soil surface
burning of crop residue on the farmland
compacting the soil surface with heavy machinery
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: covering the soil surface with organic material to reduce evaporation and erosion

Environmental Conservation.text: Strip cropping involves:
options: planting a single crop over one very large continuous area
planting crops in alternate strips along the contour to reduce soil erosion
removing topsoil in narrow strips for building construction
clearing forest in strips to create logging roads
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: planting crops in alternate strips along the contour to reduce soil erosion

Environmental Conservation.text: Rainwater harvesting as a water conservation method involves:
options: releasing stored water into rivers during the rainy season
draining of wetlands to create farmland
discharging untreated wastewater directly into rivers
collecting and storing rainwater for later use, especially during dry periods
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: collecting and storing rainwater for later use, especially during dry periods

Environmental Conservation.text: Construction of dams and reservoirs aids water conservation by:
options: releasing all stored water immediately after every rainfall
increasing the rate of water evaporation from rivers
preventing any future use of river water
storing excess water for use in irrigation, domestic supply, and during dry seasons
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: storing excess water for use in irrigation, domestic supply, and during dry seasons

Environmental Conservation.text: The main purpose of establishing wildlife/game reserves is to:
options: protect wild animals and their habitats from extinction and overexploitation
provide land exclusively for commercial farming
encourage unrestricted hunting of wild animals
promote the clearing of forests for new settlements
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: protect wild animals and their habitats from extinction and overexploitation

Environmental Conservation.text: A national park differs from a game reserve mainly in that a national park:
options: allows unrestricted logging and mining activities
is usually more strictly protected, with human activities such as hunting and settlement largely prohibited
permits large-scale commercial farming within its boundaries
has no legal protection status under the law
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: is usually more strictly protected, with human activities such as hunting and settlement largely prohibited

Environmental Conservation.text: An example of a well-known wildlife conservation area located in West Africa is:
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: Kainji National Park

Environmental Conservation.text: Recycling refers to:
options: the permanent disposal of waste materials in landfills
the burning of all waste materials
the dumping of waste into rivers and oceans
the process of converting waste materials into new, reusable products
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: the process of converting waste materials into new, reusable products

Environmental Conservation.text: One major benefit of recycling is that it:
options: increases the volume of waste sent to landfills
increases air pollution caused by waste burning
reduces the demand for raw materials and conserves natural resources
has no effect on the conservation of natural resources
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: reduces the demand for raw materials and conserves natural resources

Environmental Conservation.text: Industries can control air pollution by:
options: installing filters and scrubbers to reduce harmful emissions from chimneys
