increasing the height of chimneys without treating the emissions
burning of waste materials in the open air
discharging untreated industrial gases directly into the atmosphere
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: installing filters and scrubbers to reduce harmful emissions from chimneys

Environmental Conservation.text: Proper treatment of sewage before discharge is important because it:
options: increases the level of contaminants in rivers and streams
reduces water pollution and protects aquatic life and public health
has no impact on the quality of water bodies
encourages the spread of waterborne diseases
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: reduces water pollution and protects aquatic life and public health

Environmental Conservation.text: In Nigeria, the government agency primarily responsible for enforcing environmental protection standards is the:
options: National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency (NESREA)
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency (NESREA)

Environmental Conservation.text: A key benefit of practicing crop rotation is that it:
options: helps restore soil nutrients and reduces the build-up of pests and diseases
depletes soil nutrients faster than continuous cropping
increases the spread of pests and diseases
requires no knowledge of different crop types
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: helps restore soil nutrients and reduces the build-up of pests and diseases

Environmental Conservation.text: Mixed cropping contributes to environmental conservation by:
options: exposing bare soil to erosion throughout the year
providing continuous ground cover that reduces soil erosion and improves soil fertility
requiring the total removal of natural vegetation
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: providing continuous ground cover that reduces soil erosion and improves soil fertility

Environmental Conservation.text: Cover cropping is a conservation practice in which farmers:
options: leave the soil completely exposed after harvest
burn all vegetation before planting new crops
remove all crop residues immediately after harvest
plant fast-growing crops to cover and protect bare soil between main cropping seasons
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: plant fast-growing crops to cover and protect bare soil between main cropping seasons

Environmental Conservation.text: One major importance of environmental conservation is that it:
options: increases the rate of resource depletion
has no bearing on the survival of species
helps maintain the ecological balance necessary for the survival of living organisms
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: helps maintain the ecological balance necessary for the survival of living organisms

Environmental Conservation.text: Environmental conservation is important because it:
options: ensures that natural resources remain available for use by future generations
guarantees that resources are used up entirely by the present generation
eliminates the need for future resource management
prevents any economic use of natural resources
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: ensures that natural resources remain available for use by future generations

Environmental Conservation.text: Conservation efforts such as establishing game reserves help to:
options: reduce the number of plant and animal species in an area
protect biodiversity by preserving different plant and animal species
encourage the extinction of endangered species
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: protect biodiversity by preserving different plant and animal species

Environmental Conservation.text: Soil conservation practices are important mainly because they:
options: increase the rate of soil erosion
prevent soil degradation and maintain agricultural productivity
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: prevent soil degradation and maintain agricultural productivity

Environmental Conservation.text: Forests contribute to environmental conservation by helping to:
options: reduce rainfall in the surrounding areas
have no effect on climatic conditions
regulate climate and rainfall patterns through the water cycle
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: regulate climate and rainfall patterns through the water cycle

Environmental Conservation.text: An economic benefit derived from environmental conservation is:
options: revenue generation through eco-tourism and sustainable forestry
loss of income from tourism activities
increased cost of importing raw materials with no local benefit
reduction in employment opportunities in rural areas
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: revenue generation through eco-tourism and sustainable forestry

Environmental Conservation.text: One major problem facing environmental conservation in West Africa is:
options: excessive government funding for conservation programmes
widespread poverty, which drives people to over-exploit natural resources for survival
an oversupply of trained conservation personnel
too many strictly enforced environmental laws
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: widespread poverty, which drives people to over-exploit natural resources for survival

Environmental Conservation.text: Conservation efforts in West Africa are often hindered by:
options: overly strict enforcement of environmental laws
excessive public awareness of conservation issues
poor enforcement of existing environmental laws and regulations
abundant funding for environmental law enforcement agencies
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: poor enforcement of existing environmental laws and regulations

Environmental Conservation.text: Rapid population growth affects conservation efforts by:
options: reducing the demand for land and natural resources
decreasing the need for farmland expansion
having no effect on the use of natural resources
increasing pressure on land, forests, and water resources for settlement and farming
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: increasing pressure on land, forests, and water resources for settlement and farming

Environmental Conservation.text: A major challenge to conservation programmes in West African countries is:
options: inadequate funding to support conservation projects and enforcement agencies
excess funding leading to wasteful conservation spending
an oversupply of trained conservation personnel
a surplus of conservation equipment and infrastructure
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: inadequate funding to support conservation projects and enforcement agencies

Environmental Conservation.text: Lack of public awareness affects conservation because:
options: informed communities tend to degrade the environment more than uninformed ones
many people are unaware of the harmful consequences of environmental degradation and do not adopt conservation practices
awareness campaigns always worsen environmental problems
public education has no relationship with conservation behaviour
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: many people are unaware of the harmful consequences of environmental degradation and do not adopt conservation practices

Environmental Conservation.text: Corruption undermines conservation efforts in West Africa mainly by:
options: strengthening the enforcement of conservation laws
reducing illegal exploitation of natural resources
allowing illegal logging, poaching, and mining to continue unchecked despite existing laws
improving transparency in the management of resources
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: allowing illegal logging, poaching, and mining to continue unchecked despite existing laws

Environmental Conservation.text: Political instability in some West African countries affects conservation by:
options: guaranteeing consistent long-term funding for conservation
improving the enforcement of environmental laws
disrupting long-term environmental planning and diverting resources away from conservation programmes
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: disrupting long-term environmental planning and diverting resources away from conservation programmes

Environmental Conservation.text: A key solution to poor conservation practices is:
options: restricting all information about environmental issues from the public
discouraging community involvement in conservation activities
ignoring public opinion in conservation planning
educating the public on the importance and methods of environmental conservation
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: educating the public on the importance and methods of environmental conservation

Environmental Conservation.text: Conservation problems can be reduced by:
options: strict and consistent enforcement of environmental laws and regulations
relaxing environmental laws to encourage resource exploitation
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: strict and consistent enforcement of environmental laws and regulations

Environmental Conservation.text: Providing alternative sources of livelihood to communities near forests and reserves helps conservation by:
options: increasing their dependence on forest exploitation for income
reducing their dependence on logging, hunting, and other exploitative activities
encouraging further encroachment into protected areas
having no effect on their use of natural resources
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: reducing their dependence on logging, hunting, and other exploitative activities

Environmental Conservation.text: International cooperation helps solve conservation problems in West Africa mainly through:
options: imposing trade restrictions on all natural resources
provision of funding, technical expertise, and support for regional conservation programmes
reducing global awareness of environmental issues
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: provision of funding, technical expertise, and support for regional conservation programmes

Environmental Conservation.text: Community-based/participatory conservation approaches are effective because they:
options: exclude local communities entirely from resource management decisions
rely solely on government agencies with no local input
discourage cooperation between communities and government authorities
involve local people directly in decision-making and management of natural resources
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: involve local people directly in decision-making and management of natural resources

Environmental Conservation.text: Promoting the use of alternative energy sources, such as solar and biogas, helps conservation by:
options: reducing reliance on fuelwood and thereby lowering the rate of deforestation
increasing the demand for fuelwood among rural households
having no impact on forest resources
Environmental Conservation.correct_answer: reducing reliance on fuelwood and thereby lowering the rate of deforestation

World Population.text: The population growth rate of a country refers to:
options: the total number of people living in a country at a given time
the number of people who migrate into a country each year
the rate at which the number of people in a population increases or decreases over a given period
the ratio of males to females in a population
World Population.correct_answer: the rate at which the number of people in a population increases or decreases over a given period

World Population.text: A high birth rate contributes to rapid population growth mainly because:
options: more children are born than the number of people who die, resulting in natural increase
it leads to a higher death rate in the population
it reduces the number of people of reproductive age
it always leads to increased emigration
World Population.correct_answer: more children are born than the number of people who die, resulting in natural increase

World Population.text: Improved healthcare facilities contribute to population growth mainly by:
options: reducing death rates and increasing life expectancy
reducing the number of hospitals available to the population
World Population.correct_answer: reducing death rates and increasing life expectancy

World Population.text: Family planning and the use of contraceptives help to:
options: have no effect on population growth
reduce the birth rate and slow down population growth
increase the death rate of the population
World Population.correct_answer: reduce the birth rate and slow down population growth

World Population.text: Factors that reduce population growth include:
options: high death rates caused by diseases, famine, or war
high birth rates among the population
increased life expectancy of the population
World Population.correct_answer: high death rates caused by diseases, famine, or war

World Population.text: Compared to developing countries, developed countries generally have:
options: much higher rates of population growth than developing countries
lower rates of population growth due to lower birth rates
no recorded birth or death rates
the highest rates of natural increase in the world
World Population.correct_answer: lower rates of population growth due to lower birth rates

World Population.text: The natural increase of a population is calculated as:
options: the birth rate plus the death rate
the number of immigrants minus the number of emigrants
the birth rate minus the death rate
the total population divided by the land area
World Population.correct_answer: the birth rate minus the death rate

World Population.text: In the early/high stationary stage of the demographic transition model, a population typically has:
options: low birth rates and low death rates
high birth rates and low death rates
low birth rates and high death rates
both high birth rates and high death rates, resulting in little population growth
World Population.correct_answer: both high birth rates and high death rates, resulting in little population growth

World Population.text: The term "doubling time" in population studies refers to:
options: the time taken for a country's economy to double in size
the average age at which people in a population marry
the period between two national population censuses
the number of years it takes for a population to double in size at its current growth rate
World Population.correct_answer: the number of years it takes for a population to double in size at its current growth rate

World Population.text: Improved medical facilities generally lead to population growth by:
options: lowering infant mortality rates and increasing survival rates
increasing infant mortality rates in the population
reducing the total number of childbirths
World Population.correct_answer: lowering infant mortality rates and increasing survival rates

World Population.text: Climate is an important factor affecting population distribution because:
options: climate has no influence on where people choose to settle
extreme climates such as deserts and polar regions tend to discourage settlement
all climatic regions are equally attractive to settlers
cold polar climates always attract the highest population densities
World Population.correct_answer: extreme climates such as deserts and polar regions tend to discourage settlement

World Population.text: Relief (topography) affects population distribution because:
options: mountainous areas always have the highest population densities
relief has no effect on human settlement patterns
flat lowlands are generally easier to settle and farm than steep, rugged highlands
steep highlands are always preferred for building large cities
World Population.correct_answer: flat lowlands are generally easier to settle and farm than steep, rugged highlands

World Population.text: Fertile soils tend to attract dense population settlement mainly because they:
options: support productive agriculture, which provides food and livelihoods
prevent any form of farming activity
are usually found only in desert regions
World Population.correct_answer: support productive agriculture, which provides food and livelihoods

World Population.text: Availability of water is a major factor affecting population distribution because:
options: water availability has no bearing on where people choose to settle
areas with reliable water supply can better support human, agricultural, and industrial needs
areas with abundant water are always sparsely populated
people generally prefer to settle far away from water sources
World Population.correct_answer: areas with reliable water supply can better support human, agricultural, and industrial needs

World Population.text: Areas with many economic activities and employment opportunities tend to:
options: remain sparsely populated regardless of job availability
repel population settlement due to overcrowding concerns alone
attract dense population settlement as people migrate there for jobs
have no influence at all on population distribution
World Population.correct_answer: attract dense population settlement as people migrate there for jobs

World Population.text: Good transportation and accessibility tend to result in:
options: sparse population settlement due to increased noise levels
no significant effect on where people choose to settle
population decline in areas that are highly accessible
denser population settlement because goods, services, and people can move easily
World Population.correct_answer: denser population settlement because goods, services, and people can move easily

World Population.text: Historical and political factors, such as government policy or colonial boundaries, can affect population distribution by:
options: having absolutely no effect on where populations settle
always leading to a completely uniform population distribution
eliminating the need for any form of population planning
encouraging or restricting settlement in certain regions through planning and policy decisions
World Population.correct_answer: encouraging or restricting settlement in certain regions through planning and policy decisions

World Population.text: Population density is best defined as:
options: the average number of people living per unit area of land, usually per square kilometre
the total population of a country regardless of its land area
the rate at which a population grows each year
the number of people who migrate into an area annually
World Population.correct_answer: the average number of people living per unit area of land, usually per square kilometre

World Population.text: Sparsely populated regions of the world, such as the Sahara Desert, are typically characterized by:
options: fertile soils and abundant rainfall throughout the year
harsh climatic conditions, poor soils, and limited water supply that discourage settlement
excellent transportation networks and numerous job opportunities
mild climates that are highly attractive for farming
World Population.correct_answer: harsh climatic conditions, poor soils, and limited water supply that discourage settlement

World Population.text: Densely populated regions, such as river valleys and coastal plains, are usually characterized by:
options: fertile land, favourable climate, and good access to water and trade routes
isolation from major trade and transportation routes
World Population.correct_answer: fertile land, favourable climate, and good access to water and trade routes

World Population.text: Migration can be defined as:
options: the daily movement of people to work and back home
the movement of goods and services between countries
the seasonal movement of animals in search of pasture
the movement of people from one place to another with the intention of settling, either temporarily or permanently
World Population.correct_answer: the movement of people from one place to another with the intention of settling, either temporarily or permanently

World Population.text: Migration that occurs within the boundaries of a single country is known as:
World Population.correct_answer: internal migration

World Population.text: The movement of people from rural areas to cities in search of better opportunities is known as:
World Population.correct_answer: rural-urban migration

World Population.text: Push factors in migration refer to:
options: attractive conditions that draw people to a new location
unfavourable conditions in a place that force or encourage people to leave
government policies that prevent people from moving
the physical distance between two locations
World Population.correct_answer: unfavourable conditions in a place that force or encourage people to leave

World Population.text: Pull factors in migration refer to:
options: unfavourable conditions that drive people away from their home area
legal restrictions that prevent people from migrating
attractive conditions in a destination area that draw migrants toward it
the cost of transportation between two locations
World Population.correct_answer: attractive conditions in a destination area that draw migrants toward it

World Population.text: An example of a push factor that encourages migration is:
options: availability of good schools in the destination area
better healthcare facilities in the destination area
higher wages in the destination area
unemployment and lack of job opportunities in the home area
World Population.correct_answer: unemployment and lack of job opportunities in the home area

World Population.text: An example of a pull factor that attracts migrants to a city is:
options: drought and famine in the home area
civil war and insecurity in the home area
poor soil fertility in the home area
the availability of better job and employment opportunities
World Population.correct_answer: the availability of better job and employment opportunities

World Population.text: One negative effect of migration on the source (origin) area is:
options: an increase in the working population left behind
loss of the active/productive labour force, especially the youth
a reduction in the dependency ratio of the area
World Population.correct_answer: loss of the active/productive labour force, especially the youth

World Population.text: A major effect of migration on the destination (receiving) area is:
options: increased pressure on housing, infrastructure, and social amenities
a decrease in demand for housing and social services
reduced pressure on infrastructure and social amenities
a decline in the labour force available in the area
World Population.correct_answer: increased pressure on housing, infrastructure, and social amenities

World Population.text: One positive effect of migration on the source area is:
options: a total loss of income for the families left behind
remittances (money sent back home) which improve the living standards of families left behind
increased unemployment in the source area
a decline in living standards with no economic benefits
World Population.correct_answer: remittances (money sent back home) which improve the living standards of families left behind

World Population.text: One major challenge associated with rapid population growth is:
options: high rates of unemployment as job opportunities fail to match population increase
a shortage of available labour in most sectors of the economy
reduced competition for available job opportunities
increased wages due to a scarcity of labour
World Population.correct_answer: high rates of unemployment as job opportunities fail to match population increase

World Population.text: Rapid population growth often leads to:
options: a surplus of housing with very low occupancy rates
overcrowding and pressure on available housing
a decline in the demand for housing
automatically improved housing conditions for all citizens
World Population.correct_answer: overcrowding and pressure on available housing

World Population.text: A key challenge of high population growth in developing countries is:
options: an oversupply of schools and hospitals relative to demand
an excess supply of clean water available to all citizens
inadequate social amenities such as schools, hospitals, and clean water supply
a reduced demand for healthcare services
World Population.correct_answer: inadequate social amenities such as schools, hospitals, and clean water supply

World Population.text: Rapid population growth can lead to food insecurity mainly because:
options: food production always increases faster than the population
population growth reduces the overall demand for food
agricultural land automatically expands as population grows
food production may fail to keep pace with the rapidly increasing number of people
World Population.correct_answer: food production may fail to keep pace with the rapidly increasing number of people

World Population.text: High population growth contributes to environmental degradation mainly through:
options: reduced pressure on land and natural resources
decreased demand for fuelwood and farmland
automatically improved conservation of natural resources
increased deforestation, overgrazing, and pollution as people exploit resources to meet their needs
World Population.correct_answer: increased deforestation, overgrazing, and pollution as people exploit resources to meet their needs

World Population.text: A common consequence of rapid population growth in developing countries is:
options: a significant rise in the average income of all citizens
a reduction in the number of people living below the poverty line
an automatic improvement in the general standard of living
widespread poverty as resources and income fail to match population needs
World Population.correct_answer: widespread poverty as resources and income fail to match population needs

World Population.text: Rapid population growth places a strain on infrastructure mainly because:
options: infrastructure automatically expands to match population needs
fewer people use roads and public utilities as population grows
roads, transport systems, and utilities become overburdened by the increasing number of users
demand for transportation and utilities decreases with population growth
World Population.correct_answer: roads, transport systems, and utilities become overburdened by the increasing number of users

World Population.text: High population growth, especially with rising unemployment, is often associated with:
options: an increase in crime rates as people struggle to meet basic needs
a decrease in crime rates due to improved living conditions
no relationship between population growth and crime rates
reduced social tension in urban areas
World Population.correct_answer: an increase in crime rates as people struggle to meet basic needs

World Population.text: To manage the challenges of rapid population growth, governments often introduce:
options: policies that actively encourage higher birth rates
population control policies such as family planning programmes and public education
restrictions on access to healthcare and family planning services
policies that ban all forms of migration
World Population.correct_answer: population control policies such as family planning programmes and public education

Settlement.text: A settlement may be defined as a place where
Settlement.correct_answer: people live permanently or temporarily

Settlement.text: Which of the following is a major type of settlement based on the environment in which it is found?
Settlement.correct_answer: Rural settlement

Settlement.text: A rural settlement is best described as one in which
options: the majority of people are engaged in farming and other primary occupations
the main activity is international trade
population density is very high with skyscrapers
the majority of people are engaged in industry and commerce
Settlement.correct_answer: the majority of people are engaged in farming and other primary occupations

Settlement.text: An urban settlement is characterised mainly by
options: shifting cultivation as the main activity
high population density and non-agricultural occupations
widely spaced compounds surrounded by farmland
Settlement.correct_answer: high population density and non-agricultural occupations

Settlement.text: In a dispersed (scattered) settlement pattern, dwellings are
options: built close together around a market square
arranged in a straight line along a road
Settlement.correct_answer: widely spaced from one another

Settlement.text: A nucleated settlement pattern is one in which houses are
options: spread far apart over a wide area
strung out along a river bank only
clustered closely together around a central point
Settlement.correct_answer: clustered closely together around a central point

Settlement.text: A linear settlement pattern develops when houses are built
options: in a scattered manner with no order
in a row along a road, river or railway line
Settlement.correct_answer: in a row along a road, river or railway line

Settlement.text: Nucleated settlements commonly develop around
options: areas of poor soil requiring large farm holdings
a reliable water source or fertile farmland
Settlement.correct_answer: a reliable water source or fertile farmland

Settlement.text: Dispersed settlement patterns are most common in areas where
options: defence against enemies is the overriding concern
land is extremely scarce and fertile
a market square dominates the landscape
each farmer requires a large area of land to make a living
Settlement.correct_answer: each farmer requires a large area of land to make a living

Settlement.text: Linear settlements most typically form along
options: roads, railway lines, rivers or coastlines
Settlement.correct_answer: roads, railway lines, rivers or coastlines

Settlement.text: Which of the following is the most important factor influencing the earliest location of settlements?
Settlement.correct_answer: Availability of water supply

Settlement.text: Flat or gently sloping relief favours settlement location mainly because it
options: makes construction of buildings and roads easier
Settlement.correct_answer: makes construction of buildings and roads easier

Settlement.text: Fertile soils attract settlement because they
options: support crop cultivation which sustains the population
are found only in mountainous regions
are unsuitable for any human activity
Settlement.correct_answer: support crop cultivation which sustains the population

Settlement.text: In earlier times, some settlements were sited on hilltops mainly for the purpose of
Settlement.correct_answer: defence against enemy attack

Settlement.text: Settlements such as Jos and Enugu developed largely because of
options: the presence of exploitable mineral resources
Settlement.correct_answer: the presence of exploitable mineral resources

Settlement.text: A settlement that grows at the point where several routes meet is called a
Settlement.correct_answer: route centre or nodal settlement

Settlement.text: Which climatic condition is most likely to discourage the establishment of a settlement?
options: Extreme aridity with very little rainfall
Settlement.correct_answer: Extreme aridity with very little rainfall

Settlement.text: In settlement geography, the term "site" refers to
options: the total population of a settlement
the position of a settlement relative to other places
the actual piece of ground on which a settlement is built
the administrative status of a settlement
Settlement.correct_answer: the actual piece of ground on which a settlement is built

Settlement.text: The "situation" of a settlement describes
options: the number of rooms in each house
the exact plot of land on which houses are built
the position of the settlement in relation to surrounding areas and routes
the type of roofing material used
Settlement.correct_answer: the position of the settlement in relation to surrounding areas and routes

Settlement.text: A settlement with a good situation but a poor site would most likely face problems of
options: lack of any inhabitants at all
flooding or unstable ground for building
Settlement.correct_answer: flooding or unstable ground for building

Settlement.text: The growth of a settlement in size and population is most strongly influenced by
options: the age of its oldest building
the number of religious festivals held
natural population increase and in-migration for economic opportunities
Settlement.correct_answer: natural population increase and in-migration for economic opportunities

Settlement.text: The arrangement of settlements from the smallest to the largest in order of size and function is known as the
Settlement.correct_answer: settlement hierarchy

Settlement.text: The smallest unit in the settlement hierarchy, usually consisting of a few houses, is called a
Settlement.correct_answer: hamlet

Settlement.text: A village differs from a hamlet mainly because a village
options: has a larger population and a few basic services such as a school or market
is always larger than a city
Settlement.correct_answer: has a larger population and a few basic services such as a school or market

Settlement.text: A town can be distinguished from a village by its
options: lack of roads linking it to other places
wider range of commercial and administrative services and larger population
Settlement.correct_answer: wider range of commercial and administrative services and larger population

Settlement.text: A city is generally defined as a large urban settlement that
options: is always located in a desert
has a large population and offers high-order specialised services
Settlement.correct_answer: has a large population and offers high-order specialised services

Settlement.text: When two or more neighbouring towns and cities expand and merge into one continuous built-up area, the result is called a
Settlement.correct_answer: conurbation

Settlement.text: A very large city with a population running into several millions, exerting wide regional influence, is best described as a
Settlement.correct_answer: megacity or metropolis

Settlement.text: A settlement whose main function is to serve as the seat of government and house public offices is performing a chiefly
Settlement.correct_answer: administrative function

Settlement.text: A settlement that developed mainly as a market centre for the exchange of goods is performing a
Settlement.correct_answer: commercial function

Settlement.text: A town dominated by factories that process raw materials into finished goods is best described as having a mainly
Settlement.correct_answer: industrial function

Settlement.text: Settlements that grow around shrines, cathedrals or places of pilgrimage are said to perform a
Settlement.correct_answer: religious function

Settlement.text: A settlement noted for hosting a large university and several colleges is mainly performing a(n)
Settlement.correct_answer: educational function

Settlement.text: Most large modern cities, such as Lagos and Accra, are best described as
options: multi-functional settlements combining administrative, commercial, industrial and other roles
Settlement.correct_answer: multi-functional settlements combining administrative, commercial, industrial and other roles

Settlement.text: In urban-rural interaction, rural areas mainly supply urban centres with
Settlement.correct_answer: food, raw materials and labour

Settlement.text: In return for food and raw materials from rural areas, urban centres typically provide rural areas with
options: manufactured goods, health care and administrative services
Settlement.correct_answer: manufactured goods, health care and administrative services

Settlement.text: The movement of people from villages to cities in search of jobs, education and better amenities best illustrates
Settlement.correct_answer: rural-urban migration

Settlement.text: The exchange of goods, services and information between two large cities, such as trade between Lagos and Kano, illustrates
Settlement.correct_answer: urban-urban interaction

Settlement.text: Which of the following best describes rural-rural interaction between settlements?
options: Villages exchanging farm produce, labour and marriage relationships among themselves
A factory in a city importing raw materials from another country
A university awarding degrees to graduates
A city government making laws for a village
Settlement.correct_answer: Villages exchanging farm produce, labour and marriage relationships among themselves

Transportation.text: Transportation may be defined as the
options: movement of people, goods and services from one place to another
storage of goods in a warehouse
Transportation.correct_answer: movement of people, goods and services from one place to another

Transportation.text: Which of the following is the most flexible mode of transport for door-to-door delivery over short distances?
Transportation.correct_answer: Road transport

Transportation.text: A major advantage of railway transport over road transport is that railways can
options: carry heavy and bulky goods over long distances more cheaply
be built without any capital investment
Transportation.correct_answer: carry heavy and bulky goods over long distances more cheaply

Transportation.text: Water (marine) transport is particularly suited to carrying
options: passengers travelling within a single city
bulky and heavy cargo such as crude oil and minerals over long distances
perishable goods that must arrive within hours
Transportation.correct_answer: bulky and heavy cargo such as crude oil and minerals over long distances

Transportation.text: Which mode of transport is generally the fastest for moving people and goods over long distances?
Transportation.correct_answer: Air transport

Transportation.text: Pipelines are chiefly used for transporting
options: liquids and gases such as crude oil, refined petroleum and natural gas
bulky solid minerals like iron ore
perishable farm produce to local markets
Transportation.correct_answer: liquids and gases such as crude oil, refined petroleum and natural gas

Transportation.text: Cables, as a means of transport and communication, are mainly used to carry
Transportation.correct_answer: electricity and telecommunication signals

Transportation.text: A ropeway is a transport system best suited to
options: hilly or mountainous terrain where roads are difficult to build
Transportation.correct_answer: hilly or mountainous terrain where roads are difficult to build

Transportation.text: For moving very bulky goods such as timber and minerals over long distances, the cheapest mode of transport is usually
Transportation.correct_answer: water transport

Transportation.text: Which of the following best explains why air transport is expensive compared to other modes?
options: It carries only very small quantities of cheap goods
It does not require trained personnel
It requires large amounts of fuel and costly equipment and infrastructure
Transportation.correct_answer: It requires large amounts of fuel and costly equipment and infrastructure

Transportation.text: Efficient transportation aids economic development mainly by
options: reducing the demand for exported goods
restricting the movement of goods between regions
facilitating the movement of raw materials, finished goods and people between areas of production and consumption
Transportation.correct_answer: facilitating the movement of raw materials, finished goods and people between areas of production and consumption

Transportation.text: Transportation promotes trade primarily by
options: linking areas of surplus production to areas of demand
preventing the export of local produce
increasing the cost of every good produced
Transportation.correct_answer: linking areas of surplus production to areas of demand

Transportation.text: The spread of new farming techniques, technology and ideas from one region to another is greatly assisted by
Transportation.correct_answer: well-developed transportation and communication links

Transportation.text: Regional integration among West African countries, such as under ECOWAS, depends heavily on
options: restricting free movement of goods and people
the absence of a common transport policy
the development of road, rail and other transport links between member states
Transportation.correct_answer: the development of road, rail and other transport links between member states

Transportation.text: The Trans-West African Coastal Highway is significant mainly because it
options: links coastal countries of West Africa to promote trade and integration
was built solely for tourism in one country
replaced all railway lines in the region
Transportation.correct_answer: links coastal countries of West Africa to promote trade and integration

Transportation.text: Which of the following is a major seaport that serves as a gateway for trade in West Africa?
Transportation.correct_answer: Tema

Transportation.text: Rivers such as the Niger and Benue are important for transportation in West Africa mainly because they
options: are used exclusively for air travel
provide a means of moving goods and people, especially in the rainy season
Transportation.correct_answer: provide a means of moving goods and people, especially in the rainy season

Transportation.text: Landlocked countries like Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso depend heavily on transport links through neighbouring coastal countries mainly to
options: prevent the export of their goods
gain access to seaports for international trade
Transportation.correct_answer: gain access to seaports for international trade

Transportation.text: A major problem affecting road transport in many West African countries is
options: an oversupply of skilled road engineers
poorly maintained roads with potholes and inadequate drainage
Transportation.correct_answer: poorly maintained roads with potholes and inadequate drainage

Transportation.text: Many West African railway systems inherited from the colonial era are limited mainly because they
options: have too many interconnecting lines between countries
use only the most modern high-speed trains
were built after independence for regional integration
were designed to link mining and farming areas to the coast rather than to connect countries with one another
Transportation.correct_answer: were designed to link mining and farming areas to the coast rather than to connect countries with one another

Transportation.text: Seasonal flooding and erosion pose a major challenge to transportation in West Africa because they
options: have no effect on unpaved roads
damage roads, bridges and railway lines, disrupting movement
Transportation.correct_answer: damage roads, bridges and railway lines, disrupting movement

Transportation.text: The high cost of vehicles, spare parts and fuel in West Africa tends to
options: have no impact on transport fares
reduce the cost of transportation services
increase the cost of transportation and goods
Transportation.correct_answer: increase the cost of transportation and goods

Transportation.text: Piracy and armed robbery on some West African waterways and highways mainly result in
options: loss of goods, insecurity and reluctance of operators to use certain routes
Transportation.correct_answer: loss of goods, insecurity and reluctance of operators to use certain routes

Transportation.text: Inadequate government funding is a problem for transportation in West Africa because it leads to
options: poor maintenance and slow expansion of transport infrastructure
Transportation.correct_answer: poor maintenance and slow expansion of transport infrastructure

Transportation.text: Long delays caused by bureaucracy and multiple checkpoints at national borders in West Africa tend to
options: have no effect on transport costs
eliminate the need for customs officers
slow down the movement of goods and increase the cost of trade
Transportation.correct_answer: slow down the movement of goods and increase the cost of trade

Transportation.text: One important solution to poor transportation in West Africa is
options: increased government and private investment in infrastructure through public-private partnerships
discouraging the use of any modern vehicles
Transportation.correct_answer: increased government and private investment in infrastructure through public-private partnerships

Transportation.text: Regional cooperation among West African states can help solve transport problems mainly by
options: encouraging each country to isolate its transport network
harmonising transport policies and jointly funding cross-border infrastructure
restricting trade to domestic markets only
Transportation.correct_answer: harmonising transport policies and jointly funding cross-border infrastructure

Transportation.text: Rehabilitating and modernising old colonial railway lines would help West African transportation by
options: providing a cheaper alternative for moving bulky freight over long distances
eliminating the need for roads entirely
reducing the movement of bulky goods
Transportation.correct_answer: providing a cheaper alternative for moving bulky freight over long distances

Transportation.text: Reducing corruption and simplifying procedures at border posts would primarily help to
options: speed up the movement of goods and people across borders
reduce the volume of regional trade
discourage the use of transport routes entirely
Transportation.correct_answer: speed up the movement of goods and people across borders

Transportation.text: In transport geography, a "break of bulk point" refers to a place where
options: roads and railways are permanently closed
goods are transferred from one mode of transport to another
only passengers, never goods, are handled
Transportation.correct_answer: goods are transferred from one mode of transport to another

Transportation.text: A country that specialises in re-exporting goods brought in from other countries without significant processing is engaged in
Transportation.correct_answer: entrepot or transit trade

Transportation.text: In transportation, a "terminal" refers to
options: the end point of a transport route where goods or passengers are loaded, unloaded or transferred
Transportation.correct_answer: the end point of a transport route where goods or passengers are loaded, unloaded or transferred

Transportation.text: Feeder roads are especially important in rural West Africa because they
options: are used only for international air travel
replace the need for any market centres
connect farms and villages to major highways and markets
are built exclusively in large cities
Transportation.correct_answer: connect farms and villages to major highways and markets

Transportation.text: Containerization has improved sea transport mainly by
options: making the handling, loading and unloading of cargo faster and more secure
slowing down the loading and unloading of ships
increasing the risk of cargo damage
Transportation.correct_answer: making the handling, loading and unloading of cargo faster and more secure

Transportation.text: In Nigeria, pipelines are especially important for transporting
options: cocoa beans from farms to ports
crude oil and refined petroleum products from producing areas to refineries and depots
cattle from the north to southern markets
Transportation.correct_answer: crude oil and refined petroleum products from producing areas to refineries and depots

Transportation.text: Which of the following best describes a disadvantage of road transport compared to rail transport?
options: Road transport is generally more costly per tonne for very bulky goods over long distances and is prone to traffic congestion
Roads cannot be used by lorries
Transportation.correct_answer: Road transport is generally more costly per tonne for very bulky goods over long distances and is prone to traffic congestion

Transportation.text: Air transport is most useful in West Africa for moving
options: highly perishable goods, mail and passengers over long distances quickly
bulk minerals such as iron ore
Transportation.correct_answer: highly perishable goods, mail and passengers over long distances quickly

Transportation.text: Poor transportation networks in rural West Africa mainly contribute to
options: post-harvest losses as farm produce cannot reach markets quickly
Transportation.correct_answer: post-harvest losses as farm produce cannot reach markets quickly

Industry.text: An industry may be defined as an organised economic activity concerned with the
options: extraction, processing or manufacturing of goods and provision of services
Industry.correct_answer: extraction, processing or manufacturing of goods and provision of services

Industry.text: Industries concerned directly with the extraction of raw materials from the earth or sea, such as mining, fishing and farming, are classified as
Industry.correct_answer: primary industries

Industry.text: Secondary industries are best described as those that
options: provide only banking and insurance services
deal exclusively with the sale of land
process or manufacture raw materials into finished or semi-finished goods
extract raw materials directly from nature
Industry.correct_answer: process or manufacture raw materials into finished or semi-finished goods

Industry.text: Tertiary industries are chiefly concerned with
options: the provision of services such as banking, transport and education
the manufacture of iron and steel
Industry.correct_answer: the provision of services such as banking, transport and education

Industry.text: Which of the following is an example of a primary industrial activity?
Industry.correct_answer: Deep-sea fishing

Industry.text: Which of the following best exemplifies a secondary industrial activity?
Industry.correct_answer: Vehicle assembly in a factory

Industry.text: Which of the following is classified as a tertiary industrial activity?
Industry.correct_answer: Insurance and banking services

Industry.text: Heavy industries are best described as those that
options: use bulky raw materials and machinery to produce goods such as iron, steel and cement
are always located near residential areas because they cause no pollution
Industry.correct_answer: use bulky raw materials and machinery to produce goods such as iron, steel and cement

Industry.text: Light industries are best described as those that
options: always require huge amounts of raw materials measured in tonnes
produce relatively small, less bulky consumer goods such as textiles and electronics
are located only near iron ore deposits
process bulky ores into heavy machinery
Industry.correct_answer: produce relatively small, less bulky consumer goods such as textiles and electronics

Industry.text: Which of the following is a good example of a heavy industry?
Industry.correct_answer: Iron and steel manufacturing

Industry.text: Which of the following best illustrates a light industry?
Industry.correct_answer: An electronics assembly plant

Industry.text: Agro-based industries are industries that
options: extract crude petroleum from the ground
mine solid minerals such as tin and gold
use agricultural produce as their main raw material
Industry.correct_answer: use agricultural produce as their main raw material

Industry.text: Which of the following is an example of an agro-based industry commonly found in West Africa?
Industry.correct_answer: Cotton ginning

Industry.text: Palm oil milling and cocoa processing are classified as agro-based industries because they
options: are entirely dependent on imported machinery only
use crude oil as their main raw material
process crops produced by farmers into usable or semi-finished products
Industry.correct_answer: process crops produced by farmers into usable or semi-finished products

Industry.text: Industries whose raw materials lose a great deal of weight during processing tend to locate close to the
Industry.correct_answer: source of raw materials

Industry.text: A reliable and adequate supply of power (electricity or fuel) is important for industrial location mainly because it
options: has no effect on manufacturing costs
is needed to run machines and maintain continuous production
prevents the need for raw materials
is only relevant for agricultural activities
Industry.correct_answer: is needed to run machines and maintain continuous production

Industry.text: The availability of skilled and unskilled labour influences industrial location because industries need
options: workers solely to grow raw materials on site
labourers only for marketing finished goods abroad
workers to operate machines and carry out production processes
Industry.correct_answer: workers to operate machines and carry out production processes

Industry.text: Industries producing bulky or perishable finished goods, such as bread or soft drinks, tend to locate close to the
options: market where the goods will be sold
Industry.correct_answer: market where the goods will be sold

Industry.text: Good transport facilities influence industrial location mainly because they enable
options: the easy movement of raw materials to the factory and finished goods to the market
factories to avoid using any raw materials
Industry.correct_answer: the easy movement of raw materials to the factory and finished goods to the market

Industry.text: Availability of capital is important for industrial location because it determines
options: the ability to purchase machinery, land and raw materials, and to pay workers
the size of a country's coastline
the amount of rainfall an area receives
the religious composition of the workforce
Industry.correct_answer: the ability to purchase machinery, land and raw materials, and to pay workers

Industry.text: Government policies such as tax incentives and industrial zoning can influence industrial location by
options: having no effect on where factories are sited
encouraging or discouraging investors from setting up factories in particular areas
eliminating the need for raw materials
Industry.correct_answer: encouraging or discouraging investors from setting up factories in particular areas

Industry.text: The availability of flat, affordable land is an important factor in industrial location because it
options: is only necessary for tertiary services
is required only for railway construction
provides space for factory buildings, storage and future expansion
has no relationship with the cost of setting up a factory
Industry.correct_answer: provides space for factory buildings, storage and future expansion

Industry.text: An industry that is not tied to any particular raw material or market and can locate almost anywhere is described as
Industry.correct_answer: a footloose industry

Industry.text: A planned area set aside by government with infrastructure to accommodate several factories together is called an
Industry.correct_answer: industrial estate or industrial park

Industry.text: One major contribution of industry to economic development is that it
options: eliminates the need for foreign trade
creates employment opportunities for the population
reduces the number of jobs available in a country
Industry.correct_answer: creates employment opportunities for the population

Industry.text: Industrial development contributes to government revenue mainly through
options: the abolition of all forms of taxation
the payment of taxes and duties by industries
Industry.correct_answer: the payment of taxes and duties by industries

Industry.text: When raw materials such as cocoa beans are processed into chocolate, the industry is said to have
options: added value to the raw material
reduced the value of the raw material
Industry.correct_answer: added value to the raw material

Industry.text: Industries contribute to a country's foreign exchange earnings mainly by
options: exporting manufactured or processed goods to other countries
closing down during periods of high demand
refusing to trade with other nations
importing all their raw materials from abroad
Industry.correct_answer: exporting manufactured or processed goods to other countries

Industry.text: The growth of industries often leads to improved infrastructure in an area, such as
options: fewer roads and less electricity supply
better roads, electricity supply and water systems to support factories
the complete removal of all transport routes
Industry.correct_answer: better roads, electricity supply and water systems to support factories

Industry.text: Industrialisation contributes to import substitution mainly by
options: banning all forms of local manufacturing
increasing a country's dependence on imported goods
producing locally goods that were previously imported
Industry.correct_answer: producing locally goods that were previously imported

Industry.text: Industries contribute to technological development mainly because they
options: encourage the transfer of skills, innovation and technical know-how
prevent workers from learning new skills
have no link to research and development
Industry.correct_answer: encourage the transfer of skills, innovation and technical know-how

Industry.text: One of the major problems facing industries in West Africa is
options: too much government funding for industries
an excess of skilled industrial labour
Industry.correct_answer: inadequate and unreliable power supply

Industry.text: Poor road networks and inadequate railways affect industries in West Africa mainly by
options: making it difficult to transport raw materials and finished goods
increasing the speed of goods distribution
eliminating the need for raw materials
Industry.correct_answer: making it difficult to transport raw materials and finished goods

Industry.text: Many industries in West Africa struggle to expand mainly because of
options: inadequate capital and difficulty accessing affordable financing
Industry.correct_answer: inadequate capital and difficulty accessing affordable financing

Industry.text: A shortage of skilled manpower is a problem for industries in West Africa because it leads to
options: reliance on expensive expatriate labour or poorly trained workers
Industry.correct_answer: reliance on expensive expatriate labour or poorly trained workers

Industry.text: A small domestic market with low purchasing power affects industries in West Africa by
options: limiting the demand for locally manufactured goods
having no relationship with production levels
guaranteeing high sales for all manufactured goods
Industry.correct_answer: limiting the demand for locally manufactured goods

Industry.text: Cheap imported goods often pose a challenge to local industries in West Africa because they
options: cannot be sold within West Africa
compete favourably in price and reduce demand for locally made products
are always of much lower quality with no market appeal
encourage consumers to buy only local products
Industry.correct_answer: compete favourably in price and reduce demand for locally made products

Industry.text: Political instability and insecurity affect industrial development in West Africa mainly by
options: discouraging investment and disrupting production and supply chains
having no effect on business confidence
improving the reliability of power supply
Industry.correct_answer: discouraging investment and disrupting production and supply chains

Industry.text: One effective solution to the problem of inadequate power supply facing industries in West Africa is to
options: shut down all existing power stations
invest in diverse and reliable sources of electricity generation, including renewable energy
rely solely on firewood for industrial power
Industry.correct_answer: invest in diverse and reliable sources of electricity generation, including renewable energy

options: the abolition of money as a medium of exchange
increased efficiency and surplus production for exchange

reduces the need for any form of transportation

Trade.text: Governments generate revenue from trade mainly through the collection of
options: customs duties and taxes on imports and exports

Trade.text: Trade helps to raise the standard of living of people in a country mainly by
options: making a wider variety of goods and services available for consumption
restricting the variety of goods available

Trade.text: Trade promotes friendly relations and cooperation among countries because it
options: encourages countries to close their borders
prevents the exchange of ideas and culture
creates interdependence and regular contact between trading partners

International trade requires both countries to produce exactly the same goods

Tourism.text: Tourism can be best defined as the
options: daily movement of workers from home to office
temporary travel of people to places away from their usual environment for leisure, business or other purposes
trade in goods between two neighbouring countries
permanent movement of people to settle in a new country
Tourism.correct_answer: temporary travel of people to places away from their usual environment for leisure, business or other purposes

Tourism which involves people travelling from their home country to visit another country is referred to as

options: warm and cold springs meeting at one point

Muslims travelling to Mecca and Christians travelling to Jerusalem are examples of tourists motivated by

earning foreign exchange for the country

options: eliminates the need for local markets
generates employment opportunities for local people

infrastructure has no relationship with tourist visits
governments and investors build roads, airports and hotels to serve tourists

It leads to the total destruction of local customs
It promotes cultural exchange and understanding between people of different nations

tourists demand the demolition of historical monuments
local festivals are banned to attract foreign visitors

options: tourists buy local handicrafts and artworks as souvenirs
craft makers are banned from selling to tourists
handicrafts are only sold to government agencies
tourists never purchase locally made goods

options: taxes, levies and fees paid by tourists and tourism businesses
donations from tourists' home countries only

Nigeria Tourism and Development Issues.text: Cultural festivals such as Argungu and Osun-Osogbo attract tourists mainly because they showcase __________.

Nigeria Tourism and Development Issues.text: Which of the following is a major benefit of tourism to the Nigerian economy?

Nigeria Tourism and Development Issues.text: Which of the following is a major problem facing the tourism industry in Nigeria?

Controlled logging with replanting of trees
Indiscriminate dumping of waste into rivers

the planting of trees in an area that previously had few or none

Nigeria Tourism and Development Issues.text: Gas flaring, a common practice in the Niger Delta region, is a major cause of __________ pollution.

Nigeria Tourism and Development Issues.text: Indiscriminate dumping of industrial and household waste in Nigerian cities leads mainly to __________.

Contamination of rivers with industrial chemicals

Excessive and disturbing sound from machines, generators and traffic
Nigeria Tourism and Development Issues.correct_answer: Excessive and disturbing sound from machines, generators and traffic

Nigeria Tourism and Development Issues.text: Land reclamation refers to the process of __________.

Nigeria Tourism and Development Issues.correct_answer: converting waterlogged, swampy or submerged land into usable dry land

ECOWAS.text: ECOWAS is an acronym that stands for __________.

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: What is the main purpose of a land use survey in geographical fieldwork?
options: To record and map how land is being utilised in a given area
To measure rainfall amounts over a season
To count the population of a town
To determine the mineral content of rocks
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: To record and map how land is being utilised in a given area

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: In a land use survey, which method is commonly used to record findings directly onto a large-scale map?
options: Colour-coding or shading different land use categories on a base map
Interviewing farmers about crop prices only
Measuring wind speed at fixed intervals
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Colour-coding or shading different land use categories on a base map

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: Which of the following is a primary source of data for conducting a land use survey?
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Direct field observation and mapping

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: A base map used for carrying out a land use survey is best obtained from which of the following sources?
options: Topographical maps or aerial photographs of the study area
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Topographical maps or aerial photographs of the study area

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: Which of these is an example of a land use category typically recorded during a rural land use survey?
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Farmland, forest, and pasture

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: One major challenge students may face when conducting a land use survey is:
options: Restricted access to some private lands or properties
Absence of any land to survey
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Restricted access to some private lands or properties

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: In an urban land use survey, which of the following categories would typically be mapped?
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Residential, commercial, and industrial areas

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: A market survey in geography fieldwork is primarily conducted to study:
options: The rate of soil erosion on farmland
The speed of vehicles on a highway
The temperature variation within a forest
The pattern of goods sold, sources of goods, and buyer/seller behaviour in a market
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: The pattern of goods sold, sources of goods, and buyer/seller behaviour in a market

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: Which data collection method is most commonly used when conducting a market survey?
options: Administering questionnaires and interviews to traders and customers
Counting tree species in a forest
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Administering questionnaires and interviews to traders and customers

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: In a market survey, the term 'sphere of influence' of a market refers to:
options: The size of the market building
The area from which buyers and sellers are drawn to the market
The number of days the market operates in a week
The types of currency accepted at the market
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: The area from which buyers and sellers are drawn to the market

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: Which of the following is a typical objective of a market survey?
options: To measure the depth of gullies on a slope
To calculate rainfall intensity over a season
To determine the range and threshold of goods sold in the market
To determine traffic accident rates on a highway
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: To determine the range and threshold of goods sold in the market

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: A random sampling technique used in market surveys involves:
options: Selecting only the wealthiest traders for interview
Interviewing only relatives of the researcher
Choosing respondents based solely on the alphabetical order of their names
Selecting respondents by chance so that each has an equal opportunity of being chosen
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Selecting respondents by chance so that each has an equal opportunity of being chosen

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: One practical problem commonly encountered during market surveys is:
options: Traders' reluctance to disclose accurate sales information
Too much government funding for the survey
The complete absence of customers at any time
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Traders' reluctance to disclose accurate sales information

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: A traffic count in geographical fieldwork involves:
options: Measuring the width of a river channel
Recording the number of vehicles or pedestrians passing a fixed point over a given time
Recording rainfall totals over a month
Counting the number of shops in a market
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Recording the number of vehicles or pedestrians passing a fixed point over a given time

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: Traffic flow studies are most useful for which of the following purposes?
options: Planning road improvements and managing traffic congestion
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Planning road improvements and managing traffic congestion

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: Which instrument or method is commonly used to record traffic counts manually during fieldwork?
options: Tally charts and hand tally counters
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Tally charts and hand tally counters

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: At what times are traffic counts typically conducted in order to capture peak flow patterns?
options: During the morning and evening rush hours
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: During the morning and evening rush hours

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: A key limitation of traffic flow surveys conducted by students is:
options: Unlimited access to citywide traffic camera networks
The limited number of observation points and counting periods used
An excess of personnel available at every junction
The complete absence of vehicles to count
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: The limited number of observation points and counting periods used

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: The results of a traffic flow analysis are commonly presented using which of the following?
options: Flow-line maps or bar graphs showing vehicle volume
Pie charts showing population by age group only
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Flow-line maps or bar graphs showing vehicle volume

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: A journey-to-work study mainly investigates:
options: The seasonal migration of farmers to fertile lands
The movement of goods from farm to market
The flow of rivers from source to mouth
The daily movement of workers between their homes and places of employment
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: The daily movement of workers between their homes and places of employment

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: Which method is most appropriate for collecting data on journey-to-work patterns?
options: Questionnaires asking commuters about their origin, destination, and mode of travel
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Questionnaires asking commuters about their origin, destination, and mode of travel

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: The results of journey-to-work surveys are often illustrated using which of the following techniques?
options: Desire-line maps showing the direction and volume of commuter movement
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Desire-line maps showing the direction and volume of commuter movement

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: Journey-to-work studies are useful to urban planners mainly because they help in:
options: Planning transportation networks and reducing commuter congestion
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Planning transportation networks and reducing commuter congestion

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: Which of the following best describes 'commuting distance' as used in a journey-to-work study?
options: The total length of a country's road network
The distance between two market towns
The width of a river at its mouth
The distance travelled by a worker between home and workplace
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: The distance travelled by a worker between home and workplace

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: Which simple instrument is commonly used in the field to measure the rate of soil erosion on a slope?
options: Erosion pins (marked stakes driven into the soil)
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Erosion pins (marked stakes driven into the soil)

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: A common method of measuring soil erosion involves placing pegs at fixed points and then:
options: Counting the number of plants growing near the pegs
Recording changes in the soil surface level around the pegs over time
Measuring the temperature of the soil daily
Recording only the colour of the soil
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Recording changes in the soil surface level around the pegs over time

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: Gully erosion measurement in the field typically involves recording changes in which of the following?
options: The number of vehicles passing nearby
The types of shops in the area
The width, depth, and length of the gully over time
The prices of goods sold locally
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: The width, depth, and length of the gully over time

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: Which factor is most important to record alongside erosion-pin readings to help explain the observed rates of erosion?
options: The number of market days held in the area
The price of local building materials
The population of the nearest town
The amount and intensity of rainfall during the measurement period
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: The amount and intensity of rainfall during the measurement period

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: Sediment traps placed at the base of a slope are used in fieldwork mainly to measure:
options: The amount of soil material removed by surface runoff
The volume of traffic flow along a road
The number of daily commuters in an area
The type of goods traded in a market
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: The amount of soil material removed by surface runoff

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: One major challenge in measuring soil erosion rates over a short fieldwork period is that:
options: Erosion always happens instantly and is therefore easy to record
Erosion processes may occur slowly, making short-term changes difficult to detect
There is never any rainfall to take into account
Soil erosion cannot be measured with any instrument
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Erosion processes may occur slowly, making short-term changes difficult to detect

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: The first stage in planning any geographical fieldwork exercise should be to:
options: Define the aim and objectives of the study
Collect data randomly without a plan
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Define the aim and objectives of the study

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: Which of the following is an essential item of equipment for most geography fieldwork exercises?
options: Base maps, notebooks, and measuring instruments appropriate to the study
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Base maps, notebooks, and measuring instruments appropriate to the study

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: A 'pilot survey' conducted before the main fieldwork exercise is mainly intended to:
options: Test and refine data collection methods and questionnaires
Replace the need for any further fieldwork
Provide the final results of the whole study
Eliminate the need for a hypothesis
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Test and refine data collection methods and questionnaires

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: Which sampling method involves selecting sample points at regular, fixed intervals along a line or grid?
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Systematic sampling

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: After data has been collected during fieldwork, the next essential stage is to:
options: Repeat the same survey indefinitely without analysis
Process, analyse, and present the data using appropriate techniques
Avoid drawing any conclusions from the data
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Process, analyse, and present the data using appropriate techniques

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: Which of the following is a suitable way to present quantitative fieldwork data such as traffic counts?
options: Bar graphs, tables, or line graphs
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Bar graphs, tables, or line graphs

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: Why is it important to state a clear hypothesis before starting a fieldwork exercise?
options: It gives direction to data collection and provides a basis for testing conclusions
It guarantees that the results will always be correct
It removes the need for any data collection
It is only necessary for laboratory experiments
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: It gives direction to data collection and provides a basis for testing conclusions

Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.text: Which of the following best describes 'secondary data' as used in geography fieldwork?
options: Data collected personally through direct field measurement only
Information already collected and published by others, used to support field findings
Data that is always inaccurate and unusable
Data collected only through satellite imagery
Fieldwork Techniques in Geography.correct_answer: Information already collected and published by others, used to support field findings
